{prov}
}". ListRow.prompt.md carries a worked example with provenance={{ tier: "estimated", … }}. 3. gaps.crossCutting:
THREE CROSS-COMPONENT OBSERVATIONS, one of them a genuine law-versus-component contradiction.

1. LAW 3 AND CountBadge DISAGREE, AND NOTHING RECONCILES THEM. readme.md law 3 states unconditionally that "Every user-visible number carries a tier (`F8-01`)", and its new slot rule (added for gap 4) enumerates the hosts that satisfy it: StatCard/charts, NumberField, ListRow, AccordionItem, Block, DataTable cell, record row, RecordCard. CountBadge renders a user-visible number and is not among them, and its props carry no tier. The rule was written in the data/forms layer and the counting numeral was built in the navigation layer in a different session; neither references the other. This is the same shape as the failure the slot rule exists to prevent, one directory over. Detail in the gap 9 finding.

2. THE NEIGHBOURING COUNT COMPONENT GETS THIS RIGHT AND SAYS SO — which is evidence the two were reconciled deliberately, not by accident. readme.md:119 distinguishes them explicitly: Block's count "is **not** `CountBadge`: that component is the *unread* badge (its accessible name says \"unread\", its tone is danger), while a block's count is a total — so it groups through the market pack rather than clamping to \"99+\", and renders nothing at zero." Two components answering adjacent questions, with the difference stated. No conflict here; worth noting as the standard the CountBadge/law-3 pair has not yet met.

3. THE FIELD-MODE COMMENT'S OWN RATIOS ARE SLIGHTLY OPTIMISTIC — all still far above their floors, so this is precision, not a defect. tokens/field-mode.css annotates its overrides with ratios I recomputed as: --accent #2E1FD6 measures 9.20 (annotated 9.75), --mark-subtle #4E5257 measures 7.87 (annotated 8.14), --text-secondary #2B2D31 measures 13.79 (annotated 13.86), --text-tertiary #35383D measures 11.77 (annotated 11.73), --text-disabled #8E9299 measures 3.12 (annotated 3.09). Every one clears its floor with a large margin, and the base-scope figures in tokens/colors.css and the CountBadge figures in AppShell.jsx are exact to two decimals — so the drift is confined to the field-mode file's comments. Worth a pass if these numbers are ever quoted outward, since the rest of the system's stated ratios have proven trustworthy to the digit.

ON THE PARENT'S LISTED SORE POINTS, all five checked and four fully resolved: the 12px numeral and its contrast (fixed and measured — 12px via --fs-caption, 5.79:1 via the -text/-bg pair); --rail-w having a reader (fixed — AppRail.jsx defaults width to var(--rail-w, 72px), and --header-h/--topbar-h-mobile likewise); ghost Button/IconButton and Switch getting a field-mode edge (fixed via --control-edge, plus --track-edge for the 6px-track case where an inset ring would have made an empty slider read as full); the operator-app-never-restyled boundary (resolved in substance and re-stated correctly everywhere except one stale .d.ts prop comment in BrandColorField, detailed in gap 7).

I read every .jsx alongside its .d.ts, the .prompt.md and the @dsCard spec card for each component in this group, and both the rendered and unrendered halves of all templates touched. Two of the five gaps carry only doc-level残 issues; one (gap 9) carries a real API-versus-justification gap that does not block drawing.

gaps.component: tokens/field-mode.css second token scope + FieldModeToggle + the three edge tokens, reaching every component through the token layer
gaps.evidence:
All five round-13A findings are fixed, and two further cases were found and fixed beyond them.

FINDING 1 (ghost controls got no edge) — CLOSED. The inline "box-shadow: none" is gone from both. Button.jsx: "ghost: { bg: \"transparent\", color: \"var(--text-secondary)\", shadow: \"var(--control-edge)\", hoverShadow: \"var(--control-edge)\" }" applied as "visual = { background: hover ? \"var(--neutral-bg)\" : \"transparent\", color: v.color, boxShadow: \"var(--control-edge)\" };" with the reason on the line above: "it must not hardcode `none`, or an inline none beats field mode's rule and the lowest-contrast control in the system is the one control with no edge in sunlight." IconButton.jsx: "/* --control-edge, not a hardcoded none: see Button.jsx. */ ghost: { … shadow: \"var(--control-edge)\" }". tokens/elevation.css declares "--control-edge:none;" in the base :root, so the token resolves in both scopes.

FINDING 2 (false promise; resting ListRow) — CLOSED. ListRow.jsx now reads "boxShadow: hover ? \"var(--e2)\" : \"var(--surface-edge)\"" with "IT IS NOT HOVER-ONLY. At rest the row floats on nothing and its only edge used to be the hover shadow — and nothing in this system is hover-only." The copy was rewritten to match what ships: hint = "Darker text, and a visible edge on every card, row, field and control. For reading the screen in direct sunlight." and the source comment bounds it honestly — "It does not say \"everything\": Slider's unfilled track is still --canvas-sunken with no ring of its own".

FINDING 3 (specimen collapses when you use it) — CLOSED. field-mode.css now ships a real "[data-field-mode=\"off\"]{ … }" scope restoring all base values, and the blanket button rule was narrowed to ":not([data-field-mode=\"off\"] *)" so it cannot leak into an off subtree. guidelines/field-mode.card.html renders <Stage mode="off"/> beside <Stage mode="on"/> and states the fix: "The comparison also needs a real [data-field-mode=\"off\"] scope: custom properties inherit, so flipping the switch above used to turn the left pane into a second field-mode pane."

FINDING 4 (dead density prop) — CLOSED. Removed from both files. FieldModeToggle.d.ts's FieldModeToggleProps is now label/hint/style only; the .jsx records why: "`density` used to be declared here, defaulted, and forwarded to Switch — which has no such prop, so it was typed, documented and silently discarded. Removed rather than implemented".

FINDING 5 (reaches zero screens) — CLOSED. templates/mobile-field-app/app.jsx now surfaces it on the surveyor's own screen: "const [fieldMode, setFieldMode] = FieldModeToggle.useFieldMode();" and in MobileTopBar "actions={<ShellAction label=\"High-contrast field mode\" active={fieldMode} icon={<IcSun />} onClick={() => setFieldMode(!fieldMode)} />}" — with the same button in the unrendered Desktop() half, under "Desktop() IS NOT RENDERED — build() returns Mobile — and it is kept correct anyway, because an example nobody sees render is still an example everybody copies."

DISCLOSED SELECTOR DEVIATION — CLOSED. readme.md:318 now documents what the file actually does: "`tokens/field-mode.css` scopes the bare attribute `[data-field-mode=\"on\"]` — not `:root`, so a subtree can carry the mode and a specimen can show both at once … There is a matching `[data-field-mode=\"off\"]` scope".

TWO CASES FOUND BEYOND THE FINDINGS. Switch.jsx's track (a <span>; the real control is a visually hidden input, so no semantic selector reaches it) declares "boxShadow: error ? … : disabled ? \"none\" : \"var(--control-edge)\"" — I measured the defect it fixes: #E9ECF0 on #FFFFFF = 1.19:1. And --track-edge is an OUTSET hairline for Slider/RangeField because a 1.5px inset ring on a 6px rail "would leave a 3px core inside a dark outline, so an EMPTY slider would read as a FULL one".

MECHANISM RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. styles.css imports field-mode.css last of eleven; [data-field-mode="on"] and :root are both specificity (0,1,0), so source order decides and field mode wins. _ds_manifest.json carries all three themes: Root Expressive, Field On, Field Off. I recomputed the mode's own floors: text-secondary #2B2D31 13.79, text-tertiary #35383D 11.77, accent #2E1FD6 9.20 both directions, and --field-edge #5B6069 at 6.32/5.33/5.84 against the mode's three surfaces — comfortably over the 3:1 non-text floor.

gaps.refuteWhy:
Most of the claim reproduces. I verified independently: tokens/field-mode.css really does ship `[data-field-mode="off"]{...}` and I diffed all 27 of its declarations line-by-line against tokens/colors.css and tokens/elevation.css — every value matches the base exactly. Button.jsx ghost is `{ bg: "transparent", color: "var(--text-secondary)", shadow: "var(--control-edge)", hoverShadow: "var(--control-edge)" }` applied as `boxShadow: "var(--control-edge)"`; IconButton.jsx ghost is `shadow: "var(--control-edge)"`; ListRow.jsx is `boxShadow: hover ? "var(--e2)" : "var(--surface-edge)"`; `density` is gone from BOTH FieldModeToggle.jsx and FieldModeToggle.d.ts (FieldModeToggleProps is label/hint/style only); Switch.jsx track is `boxShadow: error ? … : disabled ? "none" : "var(--control-edge)"`; Slider.jsx/RangeField.jsx rails are `boxShadow: "var(--track-edge, none)"`; styles.css imports field-mode.css last of eleven; _ds_manifest.json registers BOTH themes (`{"selector":"[data-field-mode=\"on\"]","label":"Field On"}` and `"Field Off"`) and field-mode.css in globalCssPaths; readme.md:318 is fully rewritten; ShellAction really does take `active` (AppShell.jsx: `export function ShellAction({ label, icon, badge, onClick, active = false, style = {} })`) and sets no inline boxShadow, so it is covered by the blanket rule. Not OPEN. But four things stop it being CLOSED.

(1) THE TWO CONSUMERS THE FIX ADDED CANNOT STAY IN SYNC — AND THE TEMPLATE ASSERTS A LAW THAT IS FALSE. FieldModeToggle.jsx's whole store is `export function useFieldMode() { const [on, setOn] = React.useState(read); React.useEffect(() => { apply(on); }, [on]); return [on, setOn]; }` — no module-level store, no subscriber list, no `storage` listener, no MutationObserver. Every caller gets an independent `useState` copy whose initializer runs once. Finding 5's fix added a SECOND consumer (the shell sun button) beside the settings row that SCR-M01-11 — the one screen this gap names — exists to carry, and FieldModeToggle.d.ts describes them coexisting: "the sun button in the top bar, which is the surveyor's one-tap route, **plus this row in settings**". Render both: tap the sun → the top bar's copy goes true and `apply()` writes `<html data-field-mode="on">`, while the settings `<Switch checked={on}>` still renders unchecked against a screen that is visibly in field mode; its next tap sets its own stale state true and re-applies "on", so the switch appears dead on first press. `FieldModeToggle.set = apply` — the documented "deep link, a QA harness" route — desyncs every mounted switch identically, because it only touches the DOM and localStorage. templates/mobile-field-app/app.jsx states the opposite as fact: "FieldModeToggle.useFieldMode() is the same state the settings row writes, **so the two can never disagree**." That is the canonical template teaching a guarantee the hook does not provide. guidelines/field-mode.card.html mounts exactly one `<FieldModeToggle/>`, so no specimen exposes it.

(2) THE GHOST-CONTROL SWEEP MISSED components/data/AudioPlayer.jsx — IN A FILE THIS SAME WORK EDITED. `RoundBtn` sets `boxShadow: primary ? (hover ? "var(--e3)" : "var(--e2)") : ghost ? "none" : "var(--e1)"`, and `skip()` renders `<RoundBtn ghost size={52} label={dir < 0 ? "Back 10 seconds" : "Forward 30 seconds"}>`. Transparent background, `var(--text-secondary)` foreground, inline `box-shadow: none` — verbatim the profile Button.jsx's new comment forbids: "it must not hardcode `none`, or an inline none beats field mode's rule and the lowest-contrast control in the system is the one control with no edge in sunlight." So both 52px transport buttons on every call recording keep zero edge in field mode. The speed pill is a second instance in the same component: `boxShadow: rate === 1 ? "var(--e1)" : "none"` over `background: rate === 1 ? "var(--surface)" : "var(--accent-subtle)"` — I measured the active state at #E2DEFF on #FFFFFF = 1.30:1, with an inline `none` so neither the elevation ring nor the blanket rule reaches it. AudioPlayer was demonstrably touched by this work (it carries a full F7-16 comment and its 4px scrubber correctly reads `boxShadow: "var(--track-edge, none)"`, exactly as readme.md:123 and :318 claim) — the file was opened, the track fixed, the ghosts left. That it is an oversight rather than a ruling is clear from the contrast case: BannerAction sets the same inline `none` and documents why — "The outer button sets box-shadow:none on purpose: its rectangle is invisible, and field mode's blanket control rule would otherwise ring 44px of empty air. The visible edge belongs to the pill, which carries --e1" — AudioPlayer's ghosts have no such note and no inner pill to carry the edge.

(3) THE GAP'S OWN COMPONENT FILE CONTRADICTS ITSELF, AND THE CLAIMANT QUOTED THE STALE HALF AS PROOF OF HONESTY. FieldModeToggle.jsx's comment says "--track-edge covers the case where the inset answer would be worse than nothing: a 6px Slider or RangeField track … so it is ringed from outside instead", then four lines later "It does not say \"everything\": Slider's unfilled track is still --canvas-sunken with no ring of its own". Slider.jsx's rail is `background: "var(--canvas-sunken)", boxShadow: "var(--track-edge, none)"` — it has a ring of its own. The mangled line break ("Until that was / fixed") marks where the new text was spliced in without deleting the sentence it falsified. The claim cites that dead sentence as "the source comment bounds it honestly".

(4) EVERY ASSERTED RATIO I RECOMPUTED IS OFF (sRGB/WCAG 2.x). field-mode.css asserts `--accent:#2E1FD6; /* 9.75 on white; white on it 9.75 */` — measured 9.20:1. `--mark-subtle:#4E5257; /* 8.14 */` — 7.87:1. `--text-secondary:#2B2D31; /* 13.86 */` — 13.79:1. The Switch-track defect is stated as "about 1.15:1" in seven places (field-mode.css, Switch.jsx, Switch.d.ts, FieldModeToggle.d.ts, FieldModeToggle.prompt.md, readme.md:318, field-mode.card.html) — measured #E9ECF0 on #FFFFFF = 1.185:1 (the claimant's own 1.19 is the correct figure, so the claim and the shipped docs disagree with each other). All still clear their stated floors, so this is doc-only — but not one of the numbers reproduces. Also token-doc drift: tokens/elevation.css names only "Slider's unfilled track and RangeField's rail" as --track-edge consumers; there are four (AudioPlayer's 4px scrubber and AllocationMeter's meter track both read `var(--track-edge)`), and readme.md:318 catches only three. And Button.prompt.md ("ghost (transparent, grey hover)"), IconButton.prompt.md ("Variants: surface …, dark …, ghost") and Switch.prompt.md ("52×32 toggle. Thumb springs across; track fills accent when on.") never mention the edge at all — they do not teach the old form, but three of the five components this fix touched are silent on the fix in the file a designer actually opens.

PARTIAL. Present: the token scope, the real off scope (values verified against base), the three edge tokens wired into Button/IconButton/ListRow/Switch/Slider/RangeField/AudioPlayer/AllocationMeter, the dead prop removed on both sides, the manifest themes, the readme rewrite, and a product route in both halves of the mobile template. Missing: a shared store behind useFieldMode (two switches on one screen disagree, and the template teaches that they cannot), the ghost edge on AudioPlayer's two skip buttons and its speed pill, and internally consistent copy/numbers on the gap's own component.

gaps.component: TenantHeader + TenantMark (the page-level logo carrier) inside CustomerSurface's token scope
gaps.evidence:
THE MISSING NOUN NOW EXISTS. components/brand/TenantHeader.jsx is a real file exporting both halves, and _ds_manifest.json confirms it compiled: {"name":"TenantMark","sourcePath":"components/brand/TenantHeader.jsx"} and {"name":"TenantHeader",…}. The logo has a first-class prop — TenantHeader.d.ts: "/** The tenant's logo: a URL string, or a ready node. Omit and the monogram renders. */ logo?: string | React.ReactNode;" — and TenantHeader is documented as exactly what the gap asked for: "The page-level identity band for a **customer link page** — the header `CustomerSurface`'s canonical example promised and the system did not have. `F5-39` makes the link page the path of record, so those five screens (`SCR-F5-01`…`-05`) are whole pages of ordinary components rather than documents; `DocumentPreview`'s A4 frame was the only place a tenant logo could appear."

THE CANONICAL EXAMPLE NO LONGER REFERENCES A NON-EXISTENT COMPONENT. CustomerSurface.prompt.md gained a section headed "## The colour is here; the LOGO is `TenantHeader`" and its snippet now resolves: "<CustomerSurface brandColor={tenant.brandColor} tenantName={tenant.name} as=\"main\" fullHeight>" / "  <TenantHeader logo={tenant.logoUrl} name={tenant.name} caption=\"Your solar proposal · 8.4 kWp · Kothrud, Pune\" />".

THE OPERATOR BOUNDARY IS ENFORCED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY CONVENTION. TenantMark's monogram reads "background: \"var(--tenant-mark, var(--neutral-bg))\"" and --tenant-mark is emitted only by CustomerSurface.tenantTokens(), inline on its own node — so the same component is tenant-coloured on a link page and neutral in the operator chrome with no prop and no branch.

I RECOMPUTED THE CONTRAST GATE rather than accepting it. CustomerSurface.jsx: "const markBg = onBrand.passes ? brand : ink;". For the case the docs name, #006FFF, I measure white-on-it 4.45:1 and near-black-on-it 4.45:1 — both under the floor, so bestTextOn().passes is correctly false and the monogram falls back to ink. The prompt's stated result #0056C6 measures 6.67:1 on paper and 6.67:1 for white on it (symmetric, as the docstring argues).

THE LAWS THAT FORBADE THIS WERE REWRITTEN. readme.md:143 now scopes DocumentPreview to "the boundary of `F7-07`'s **document** half only: what the frame bounds is the proposal, and what bounds the tenant *colour* is `CustomerSurface`'s subtree. Reading the frame as the whole law is what left the link pages … unbranded for a round." readme.md:140's brand inventory now lists TenantMark and TenantHeader. BrandColorField.d.ts's docblock was corrected to "**It never restyles the operator app.** … The colour reaches two surfaces once saved: the generated proposal (`DocumentPreview`) and the tokenised customer-link pages (`CustomerSurface`), and nothing else."

A SPEC CARD DEMONSTRATES THE THREE-WAY BOUNDARY. tenant-branding.card.html (@dsCard name="Tenant branding scope") renders the document, the link page and the operator app side by side with a live swatch picker, mounts TenantHeader with a real asset (assets/tenant-suryodaya-logo.svg, present in the project), and prints the resolved tokens so the gate is shown rather than asserted.
gaps.stillMissing:
One stale sentence, in the file the gap named as the blocking doc. BrandColorField.d.ts still carries on its `helper` prop:

  "/** Defaults to the F7-07 statement: documents only, the app is never restyled. */"

"documents only" is the pre-fix half-scope statement, and it now misdescribes its own default. BrandColorField.jsx's actual default is correct and names both surfaces:

  helper = "Used on the proposal PDF and the customer link page. The HelioGrid app itself is never restyled."

So the shipped user-facing string is right and only the .d.ts comment describing it is wrong — but the .d.ts is the surface an implementer reads for the API, and this is the same file whose "documents only" framing the original audit quoted as the law forbidding the fix. The .jsx's own header comment is already correct ("the brand colour rides the generated proposal and the customer link page"), which makes this the last line in the component still teaching the old scope.

gaps.component: EditorSurface (+ useEditorForm), with modal support added to Sheet and DetailPanel
gaps.evidence:
THE SWITCH MEASURES ITS OWN LAYER, not the viewport — verified in EditorSurface.jsx, not just claimed. The probe is placed in the overlay's own coordinate space and read by rect, and `window.innerWidth` appears nowhere in the file: `position: inset ? "absolute" : "fixed", left: 0, right: 0, top: 0, height: 0` with `const read = () => setW(el.getBoundingClientRect().width)`, then `const panel = layerW == null ? null : layerW >= panelAbove;` and `if (!open || panel == null) return probe;` — so nothing is drawn before the first measurement and no frame is swapped after.

THE NON-MODAL VARIANT IS REAL IN BOTH FORMS, which is the half that could have been faked by passing a prop nothing consumed. EditorSurface passes `modal={modal}` down, and both receivers honour it. Sheet.jsx: `{modal && <SheetBackdrop onClick={dismissible ? onClose : undefined} .../>}`; `if (!modal || e.key !== "Tab" || !panelRef.current) return;`; `if (modal && !inset) { prev = document.body.style.overflow; document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"; }`; `aria-modal={modal ? "true" : undefined}`. DetailPanel.jsx carries the identical four gates. So backdrop, focus trap and scroll lock genuinely drop together.

THE TWO DOCSTRINGS THE AUDIT QUOTED ARE GONE. Sheet.d.ts no longer says only "Traps focus" — it now reads: "**Modal by default.** `false` drops the backdrop, the focus trap and the scroll lock together — the three are one decision. Use it only through `EditorSurface`." DetailPanel.d.ts's "Same backdrop law as Sheet" now continues: "`modal={false}` drops backdrop, focus trap and scroll lock together." Both also redirect authorship: "**An editor mounts `EditorSurface`, not this.**"

readme.md states it as system law twice — line 149 ("the law is the **switch**… The measurement is the **width of the layer the editor mounts into** — a zero-height probe in the overlay's own coordinate space, never `window.innerWidth`") and inside law 4's own-width rule ("**The sheet-versus-panel switch obeys the same law and is owned by `EditorSurface`**… No screen performs that switch itself").

The canonical example performs both halves: editor-surface.card.html renders the same `<EditorSurface>` call in a 375px layer and a wide layer, and demos `<EditorSurface inset open modal={false} title="Setback" …>` driving a ring that repaints from `Slider`'s `onInput` — the exact MS3-27 case the gap was written for.
gaps.crossCutting:
Three neighbour-level issues, all found by reading implementations against the docstrings that describe them.

1. DetailPanel.jsx ADVERTISES A RESPONSIVE BEHAVIOUR IT DOES NOT HAVE — and it is the panel half of gap 14's switch, so it sits directly under the law gap 14 established. Its file header claims: "Added: own-width responsiveness (a panel narrower than 560px switches to the phone answer — full-bleed, stacked actions), states, density." No such code exists in the file. There is no ResizeObserver, no width measurement of any kind, and no occurrence of 560 — the only sizing is `width: "min(" + width + "px, 100%)"`. This directly contradicts readme.md law 4 ("Own-width, never viewport… a component that owns a breakpoint has to publish it"), which is the law gap 14 leans on. Harmless when mounted through EditorSurface (the panel form is only chosen at ≥720px of layer width), but DetailPanel is explicitly sanctioned for direct use — "Mount `DetailPanel` directly for a drawer that is a drawer at every width — the records master-detail" — and that is exactly the caller the stale claim misleads. Either implement the 560px answer or delete the clause.

2. THE minScale CROP CLAIM IS ARITHMETICALLY WRONG AT THE WIDTH IT NAMES (detailed under gap 26). It is worth flagging as cross-cutting because it is repeated verbatim on three independent surfaces — PreviewFrame.d.ts, PreviewFrame.jsx's header, and readme.md law 6 — plus the card's closing note. A reader checking any one of them gets the same false guarantee, which is the multi-surface propagation pattern this audit was set up to catch.

3. A SMALL FONT-SIZE DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN RichTextView AND ITS ONE IN-PRODUCT CALLER. RichTextView's type says: "Base size. 14 on screen, 11 inside a `DocumentPreview` sheet. Never below 12 on screen." DocumentPreview.jsx calls it with `fontSize={10}` — `<RichTextView value={terms} logoSrc={logoSrc} logoLabel={logoLabel} fontSize={10} …/>` — not the documented 11. Minor, and it is document type rather than screen type so the "never below 12 on screen" floor is not breached, but the component's stated calibration and its only caller should agree, particularly since that 10px is then scaled again by PreviewFrame (10 × ~0.71 = ~7.1px in the M01-19 preview) — which compounds issue 2 above.

NO CONTRADICTIONS FOUND BETWEEN THE FIVE COMPONENTS THEMSELVES. The three places where two of these gaps could have answered the same question twice are each resolved by one deferring to the other rather than duplicating: FilterPanel mounts EditorSurface rather than re-deciding sheet-vs-panel ("filtering inherits `F7-21`'s switch instead of answering it a second time"); DocumentPreview's terms band renders through RichTextView rather than growing its own renderer; and the override/attribution/provenance axes are kept to three mutually exclusive slots with the hosts enforcing exclusivity in code (`const attr = !gap && !ov && col.attribution ? …`), not merely in prose. FilterChips and FacetChips coexist deliberately with a stated boundary and genuinely different keyboard models (tablist/aria-selected with arrow-selects, versus group/aria-pressed with arrow-moves-only), which is a correct split rather than a second treatment of one idea.
gaps.refuteWhy:
CORE LANDED (verified, not taken on trust): EditorSurface.jsx really performs the switch off a probe in the overlay's own coordinate space — `const panel = layerW == null ? null : layerW >= panelAbove;` and `if (!open || panel == null) return probe;` with `position: inset ? "absolute" : "fixed"` and `const read = () => setW(el.getBoundingClientRect().width)`; `window.innerWidth` is absent. `modal` is genuinely consumed: Sheet.jsx has all four gates (`{modal && <SheetBackdrop .../>}`, `if (!modal || e.key !== "Tab" ...)`, `if (modal && !inset) { ... document.body.style.overflow = "hidden"; }`, `aria-modal={modal ? "true" : undefined}`). FilterPanel.jsx mounts EditorSurface; both templates use it in BOTH halves including the never-rendered ones; SKILL.md, readme lines 148-150/182, _adherence.oxlintrc.json (modal listed on all three) and _ds_manifest.json agree. 720 matches Kanban per readme law 4.

REFUTED ON THREE COUNTS.

(1) MODAL STILL TEACHES THE CALLER-PERFORMED SWITCH — the claimant never opened it. Modal.jsx header: "Use for decisions that need a straight answer; use Sheet on mobile and DetailPanel for records you browse." Modal.d.ts: "On mobile prefer Sheet; use Modal on desktop." Modal.prompt.md: "On mobile use `Sheet` instead; Modal is the desktop form." That is precisely what readme line 182 now forbids ("No screen performs that switch itself") and what the gap was written to kill. It is in scope: the register's nineteen surfaces explicitly name "the cancel confirm, the waive dialog, the reversal confirm, the record-payment sheet, the typed denial sheet" — decisions, Modal's declared job. Modal.jsx has no `modal` prop, hard-codes `aria-modal="true"`, always renders `SheetBackdrop`, and is unreachable from EditorSurface (which renders only Sheet or DetailPanel). Sheet.prompt.md/.d.ts and DetailPanel.prompt.md/.d.ts each gained "An editor mounts `EditorSurface`, not this."; Modal gained nothing. Worse, Modal.prompt.md's second canonical example is "Form modal — assign a surveyor" with two <Input>s — the assign picker from the register's own list — mounted on Modal with instructions to hand-swap on mobile; panels.card.html renders the same Modal confirm as its spec card with no EditorSurface on it.

(2) A README LAW CONTRADICTS THE CHANGE. The claim "the two docstrings the audit quoted are gone" is true of the .d.ts files, but a third copy survives as system law at readme.md line 34: "`Sheet`/`Modal`/`DetailPanel` trap focus and restore it" — stated as universal keyboard parity, no modal={false} carve-out, against line 150's "no focus trap".

(3) A .d.ts/.jsx DISAGREEMENT INTRODUCED BY THIS CHANGE. "DetailPanel.jsx carries the identical four gates" is false — it carries three. There is no `document.body.style.overflow` anywhere in DetailPanel.jsx; the effect cleanup is only removeEventListener plus focus restore. Yet the new DetailPanel.d.ts says "`false` drops backdrop, focus trap and scroll lock together" and readme line 150 makes "the three are one decision" law. On the desktop half — what a studio inspector at >=720px actually gets — the law is two-thirds implemented, and a modal DetailPanel lets the page scroll behind it.

ALSO: DetailPanel.jsx's header and DetailPanel.prompt.md publish a 560px own-width rule ("Below 560px of its own width it fills the container") the file never measures — only `width: "min(" + width + "px, 100%)"` — a fourth breakpoint number in prose beside EditorSurface's real 720.

A NUMERIC CLAIM THAT DOES NOT HOLD, repeated on three teaching surfaces. PreviewFrame.d.ts: "**375px, honestly.** An A4 sheet at 335px is 0.70 scale, which puts 11px document type at ~7.7px. The frame refuses to scale below `minScale` and **crops** instead." readme.md law 6 asserts the consequence directly: "below `minScale` the frame **crops to the readable top** rather than shrinking — at 375px a scaled A4 sheet would put 11px document type at about 7.7px."

Computed from the code, the crop never fires at 375px. `const raw = Math.min(1, w / designWidth); const cropped = raw < minScale; const scale = cropped ? minScale : raw;` with `minScale = 0.62` and `designWidth = 480` (DocumentPreview's `DESIGN_W`, and the value the card passes). At a 375px phone the frame's own width is ~335–343px, so raw = 335/480 = 0.698 or 343/480 = 0.715 — both comfortably ABOVE 0.62, so `cropped` is false, the sheet scales, and 11px type renders at 7.68–7.86px: exactly the size the docs call unacceptable. The crop only triggers below 480 × 0.62 = 297.6px of frame width, which no phone layout reaches. The caption's "Showing the top, at a size you can read." therefore never renders on the screen the guarantee was written for.

The floor is also looser than the case that motivates it: 0.62 permits 6.82px type, smaller than the 7.7px the rationale rejects. Either `minScale` needs to rise above ~0.72 for a 480px subject, or the three surfaces should stop promising a crop at 375px. The gap's own requirement is unaffected — this is a self-inflicted legibility claim on the same component.

gaps.component: RichText + RichTextView with measure() and a pageEstimate slot, filled by PagedDocument's PageEstimate
gaps.evidence:
ALL SIX OF THE REGISTER'S NAMED REQUIREMENTS LAND.

(4) A RENDERER, NOT ONLY AN EDITOR — `RichTextView` ships in the same file and every mark has a defined read-only rendering, enforced rather than promised: the closed set is `RichTextSpan { text, b?, i?, href? }` plus `p | h | ul | ol | logo`, and `spansFrom`/`serialise` whitelist by tag so "a paste from Word cannot smuggle a font into a customer's document." (5) THE INLINE LOGO exists as a real block — `{type:"logo"}`, with `toggleLogo()` and `onLogoChange`. (6) THE TEMPLATE ROUND-TRIP is `templates` / `onLoadTemplate` / `onSaveAsTemplate`, and the value is "**A block list, not HTML**" precisely so it round-trips into M01-51's tenant template set and is shared with SCR-M01-19's T&C body — which DocumentPreview confirms by typing its own `terms?: RichTextValue`.

(3) DESIGN AT THE CAP: `minHeight = 260` default with the prompt directing "`minHeight` 300+ for the builder's step 9 — three pages of text and translation expansion, not a two-line box", and the card renders `minHeight={300}` against five real blocks.

(2) THE COUPLING TO THE PAGE SURFACE IS GENUINE, which was the one claim most able to be false — four teaching surfaces assert that `PageEstimate` comes from `PagedDocument.jsx`, so I opened that file. Both symbols really are exported there: `export function estimatePages(metrics, opts = {})` and `export function PageEstimate({ metrics, measured, max, style = {}, ...opts })`, computed against the same module's `PAGE_GEOMETRY = { a4: { w: 794, h: 1123, … } }`, plus `PagedDocument.estimate = estimatePages; PagedDocument.PageEstimate = PageEstimate;`. The arithmetic is honest about its one assumption (`MEAN_ADVANCE_EM = 0.5`, "the one figure in estimatePages() that is measured from type rather than derived from geometry") and returns `basis` so a reader can check it.

The seam's contract is honoured on both sides: `pageEstimate` renders `{pageEstimate}` verbatim in the footer beside a real character count, so an empty slot renders nothing rather than "≈ 1 page"; `PageEstimate` returns `if (!n) return null;` at zero characters and drops the "≈" only under `measured` (`{measured != null ? word : `≈ ${word}`}`), with the cap stated in words (`· {n - max} over the {max}-page limit`). `measure()` reads the value, never the DOM.

rich-text.card.html wires the real thing — `pageEstimate={<PageEstimate metrics={m} max={3} paper="a4" contentWidth={698} fontSize={16}/>}` — and shows the same value rendered three ways: the editor, `RichTextView` on screen, and inside a `DocumentPreview` `parts={["cover","terms"]}` sheet.

gaps.crossCutting:
Four cross-cutting observations, in descending order of what they cost the 99 screens.

1. AN UNCERTIFIED THIRD BACKGROUND - TOKEN-LAYER, AND IT REACHES MORE THAN MY GROUP. tokens/colors.css states its own contract in its header: "Every token that sets WORDS clears 4.5:1 on BOTH #FFFFFF and #F6F7F9. The canvas is the harder background; a text colour has to pass on both." I recomputed every ratio in that file and they are all correct (--text-tertiary #6B6E74 measures 5.112 on white and 4.769 on canvas against the stated 5.11 / 4.77). But --canvas-sunken (#EEF0F3) is a third background the file never certifies, and components paint 12px --text-tertiary words on it: SourceDocument's `Message` in its `unsupported` and `empty` states measures 4.478:1. That is a token-layer decision with a token-layer fix (either certify --text-tertiary against --canvas-sunken and accept 4.48, or state that words on a sunken well take --text-secondary, which measures 6.433:1 there). Left as it is, every screen that puts quiet text on a sunken well re-decides it. This is the only numeric claim in my group that did not survive recomputation.

2. THE SYSTEM HAS TWO ANSWERS TO "AN UNAVAILABLE CONTROL EXPLAINS ITSELF", AND THEY CONTRADICT. Menu.jsx and OptionCardGroup.jsx deliberately refuse native `disabled` so the reason stays hearable - Menu: `disabled={it.disabled && !reason} aria-disabled={it.disabled || undefined}` with the comment "An item with a stated reason STAYS IN THE ARROW-KEY WALK ... because a skipped item is one whose reason a keyboard user can never hear"; OptionCardGroup does the same and even walks onto it (`while (options[t].disabled && !options[t].disabledReason ...)`). DateSet follows the same rule per readme line 94 ("A pack date in the grid is `aria-disabled`, **stays focusable**"). But ReorderList's end arrows and Tabs' `disabled` tab both use native `disabled`, which removes them from the tab order - and in ReorderList that is exactly what makes its documented "already first" announcement unreachable (finding 40). Same principle, two implementations, one of them producing a documented-but-dead behaviour. Worth one ruling before 99 screens copy whichever they meet first.

3. `meta` HOLDS AS A LAW BUT IS ENFORCED BY TYPE IN ONLY FIVE OF SIX HOSTS. readme.md law 7 says meta is "a count or a status, in one line of text" and "never carries a mark, a tier or a total", and I confirmed that in every host: Accordion, Menu, OptionCardItem, SourceDocument, NextAction and TenantMark all type it `string`, and Accordion/Menu carve the excluded cases out in their own docstrings ("**Not a tier**, and not a total" / "**Not a mark**: use `marks`"). The exception is RecordCard, whose `meta?: React.ReactNode[]` renders mono middot-joined parts. It is unchanged from before this round and the card, the prompt.md and all three templates only ever pass strings, so nothing teaches the wrong thing - but it is the one host whose type would accept a Badge, and it is also the host whose whole gap was "this row cannot carry two facts". Tightening to `(string | number)[]` would make law 7 structural everywhere.

4. TWO GROUPED-TOKEN OVERFLOW TREATMENTS NOW COEXIST, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE - recorded so it is not re-litigated. ChipGroup's "+N" is an expandable 44px pill that reveals in place; AvatarGroup's is a static overlap circle with no `label`, no `empty` and no expansion (Avatar.d.ts: `AvatarGroupProps { people, size, max }`). ChipGroup.jsx and readme line 108 both give the reason - AvatarGroup "takes PEOPLE, not labels, and its whole grammar (overlap, +N circle, faces) is wrong for words" - so this reads as a settled split rather than a second answer to one question. No action needed; flagged only because a reviewer scanning for duplicate treatments will land on it.

No other contradiction found between my five and their neighbours: FieldOverride vs ValueSource is exclusive and host-enforced in three separate files; MarkRow vs ChipGroup is split on host-is-a-control vs host-is-a-cell and stated identically in the .jsx, the .d.ts, the prompt.md and readme law 7; ReorderList vs Timeline vs Kanban.onMove vs DataTable.sortable keep four distinct jobs; SourceDocument vs PreviewFrame vs DocumentPreview vs Dropzone are separated on operability in all four of their docs. Most of the claim survives. Teaching surfaces agree: ValueSource.prompt.md (unread by the claimant) carries the same three-row table and repeats the strikethrough decline; readme.md law 8 declines it verbatim; SKILL.md's slot law says "which layer supplied an un-overridden value in `attribution` (`ValueSource` — never both at once)"; DataTable.prompt.md has a "Which layer supplied a cell's value" section; FieldOverride.prompt.md/.d.ts both cede the axis. Textarea.jsx really does render it (`{attribution && ...renderAttribution(...)}`) and Textarea.prompt.md teaches the "Falling back to Hindi" case. Contrast recomputed from tokens/colors.css: --text-tertiary #6B6E74 on --surface = 5.11:1 and on --canvas #F6F7F9 = 4.77:1, both ≥4.5 at 12px. ValueSource is in _ds_manifest.json and attribution.card.html is a registered card.

BUT the MS10-13 half — one of gap 39's three bound PRD rows, and the register's own second requirement ("'yours X · design now Y' — both values shown") — carries a defect the claim did not look for, because it never opened FieldOverride.d.ts and never read the stale branch's button labels. FieldOverride.jsx: `<LinkButton onClick={onReset} label={fieldName ? `Reset ${fieldName} to ${stale ? newValue : autoValue}` : undefined}>{stale ? "Keep mine" : ...}</LinkButton>`. In `stale`, `autoValue` is "yours" and `newValue` is "design now"; `onReset` is documented in FieldOverride.prompt.md's own example as `onReset:keepMine, onTake:takeNew` and in readme.md as "the user may still want their own number". So with `{state:"stale", autoValue:"16", newValue:"19", fieldName:"Module count"}` the two adjacent buttons announce: onTake → "Take the new value for Module count: 19", onReset → "Reset Module count to 19" — both name 19, and the second one keeps 16. The visible label "Keep mine" is not contained in the accessible name at all (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name), and the accessible name states the exact opposite of the act. FieldOverride.d.ts and the .jsx disagree on this line: the d.ts says `fieldName` is "Named in the buttons' accessible labels, so a screen reader hears which field it restores" — it hears the value it does not restore. This is inside the shared component, so all 99 screens inherit it and no drawing-time choice can fix it.

Two lesser residues. (1) The two hosts SCR-M01-15's rates panel is actually built from teach nothing about the slot in their own prompt files: NumberField.prompt.md — a long, freshly-revised doc with full sections on money mode and `error` — never mentions `attribution` or `override`, and Input.prompt.md mentions neither either; only their .d.ts files, ValueSource.prompt.md, attribution.card.html, readme law 8 and SKILL.md carry it. (2) SKILL.md elevates `attribution` to a system-wide slot law, but Image.d.ts already owns the word for something else: `attribution?: string` — "Who took it — the shadow set captions each shot with a name and a date/hour" — so a designer obeying the slot law on an ImageFrame passes a ValueSource spec into a photo-credit string. Neither of these blocks SCR-M01-15, but with a confirmed .d.ts/.jsx contradiction in the MS10-13 half the clean CLOSED does not stand.

gaps.crossCutting:
Four cross-cutting observations, in descending order of what they cost the 99 screens.

1. AN UNCERTIFIED THIRD BACKGROUND - TOKEN-LAYER, AND IT REACHES MORE THAN MY GROUP. tokens/colors.css states its own contract in its header: "Every token that sets WORDS clears 4.5:1 on BOTH #FFFFFF and #F6F7F9. The canvas is the harder background; a text colour has to pass on both." I recomputed every ratio in that file and they are all correct (--text-tertiary #6B6E74 measures 5.112 on white and 4.769 on canvas against the stated 5.11 / 4.77). But --canvas-sunken (#EEF0F3) is a third background the file never certifies, and components paint 12px --text-tertiary words on it: SourceDocument's `Message` in its `unsupported` and `empty` states measures 4.478:1. That is a token-layer decision with a token-layer fix (either certify --text-tertiary against --canvas-sunken and accept 4.48, or state that words on a sunken well take --text-secondary, which measures 6.433:1 there). Left as it is, every screen that puts quiet text on a sunken well re-decides it. This is the only numeric claim in my group that did not survive recomputation.

2. THE SYSTEM HAS TWO ANSWERS TO "AN UNAVAILABLE CONTROL EXPLAINS ITSELF", AND THEY CONTRADICT. Menu.jsx and OptionCardGroup.jsx deliberately refuse native `disabled` so the reason stays hearable - Menu: `disabled={it.disabled && !reason} aria-disabled={it.disabled || undefined}` with the comment "An item with a stated reason STAYS IN THE ARROW-KEY WALK ... because a skipped item is one whose reason a keyboard user can never hear"; OptionCardGroup does the same and even walks onto it (`while (options[t].disabled && !options[t].disabledReason ...)`). DateSet follows the same rule per readme line 94 ("A pack date in the grid is `aria-disabled`, **stays focusable**"). But ReorderList's end arrows and Tabs' `disabled` tab both use native `disabled`, which removes them from the tab order - and in ReorderList that is exactly what makes its documented "already first" announcement unreachable (finding 40). Same principle, two implementations, one of them producing a documented-but-dead behaviour. Worth one ruling before 99 screens copy whichever they meet first.

3. `meta` HOLDS AS A LAW BUT IS ENFORCED BY TYPE IN ONLY FIVE OF SIX HOSTS. readme.md law 7 says meta is "a count or a status, in one line of text" and "never carries a mark, a tier or a total", and I confirmed that in every host: Accordion, Menu, OptionCardItem, SourceDocument, NextAction and TenantMark all type it `string`, and Accordion/Menu carve the excluded cases out in their own docstrings ("**Not a tier**, and not a total" / "**Not a mark**: use `marks`"). The exception is RecordCard, whose `meta?: React.ReactNode[]` renders mono middot-joined parts. It is unchanged from before this round and the card, the prompt.md and all three templates only ever pass strings, so nothing teaches the wrong thing - but it is the one host whose type would accept a Badge, and it is also the host whose whole gap was "this row cannot carry two facts". Tightening to `(string | number)[]` would make law 7 structural everywhere.

4. TWO GROUPED-TOKEN OVERFLOW TREATMENTS NOW COEXIST, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE - recorded so it is not re-litigated. ChipGroup's "+N" is an expandable 44px pill that reveals in place; AvatarGroup's is a static overlap circle with no `label`, no `empty` and no expansion (Avatar.d.ts: `AvatarGroupProps { people, size, max }`). ChipGroup.jsx and readme line 108 both give the reason - AvatarGroup "takes PEOPLE, not labels, and its whole grammar (overlap, +N circle, faces) is wrong for words" - so this reads as a settled split rather than a second answer to one question. No action needed; flagged only because a reviewer scanning for duplicate treatments will land on it.

No other contradiction found between my five and their neighbours: FieldOverride vs ValueSource is exclusive and host-enforced in three separate files; MarkRow vs ChipGroup is split on host-is-a-control vs host-is-a-cell and stated identically in the .jsx, the .d.ts, the prompt.md and readme law 7; ReorderList vs Timeline vs Kanban.onMove vs DataTable.sortable keep four distinct jobs; SourceDocument vs PreviewFrame vs DocumentPreview vs Dropzone are separated on operability in all four of their docs. I also confirmed every new export is actually in the shipped bundle (_ds_manifest.json lists SourceDocument, ReadAlongside, ChipGroup, MarkRow, ReorderList, ValueSource and RecordCard), and that the two sibling templates (desktop-web-app, mobile-field-app) teach nothing stale in their unrendered halves - their leads data simply carries no flags, so they use RecordCard without `marks` rather than with an old API.

gaps.refuteWhy:
Most of their evidence survives re-reading. In `components/data/ChipGroup.jsx` overflow really is by count (`const capped = max > 0 && all.length > max; const shown = capped && !open ? all.slice(0, max) : all;`), the "+N" really is a control (`aria-expanded={open}` … `height: 44, minWidth: 44, margin: `${(h - 44) / 2}px 0``), the empty rule really is code (`if (all.length === 0) return empty;`), and readme.md:30 really does record the defect it fixes ("a pill 6px too narrow (`ChipGroup`'s \"+N\", **38.1**×44)"). I re-measured the pill: 24px padding + "+9" at 13px ≈ 38.3, so 38.1 was right and `minWidth: 44` closes it; the negative margin (expressive −8, functional −10) keeps the 28/24px line height, and `TD = { … height: D.rowH … }` makes rowH a genuine floor. `_ds_manifest.json` exports `ChipGroup` and `MarkRow` and registers `marks-and-chips.card.html`; SKILL.md and readme.md:108 state the same rule. But "TEACHING SURFACES AGREE" is false, and the cell half is not honoured at both sizes in the way its own docs promise. 1. `column.wrap` is silently a no-op on three of the four stacked-card slots — the twin-call-site failure, inside the very pair they cite. `components/data/DataTable.jsx:445` filters `const rest = columns.filter((c) => c !== primary && c !== secondary && c !== trailing && !c.hideStacked);` and ONLY the `rest` branch reads `wrap`: line 490 `
`. The other three slots read `isLive` alone — line 476 `...(isLive(primary) ? TAPPABLE : null)`, line 477 `...(isLive(trailing) ? TAPPABLE : null)`, line 479 `...(isLive(secondary) ? TAPPABLE : null)`. So a `wrap` column that is also `secondary` (documented as "Sits under the title when stacked" — the natural home for a roles/flags cell) gets neither the full-width label-above treatment nor `pointerEvents: "auto"`, and since the content wrapper is `pointerEvents: onRowClick ? "none" : undefined` (line 475), the "+N" becomes **untappable on the phone** on any clickable row. They correctly called the `TAPPABLE` on a wrap cell "load-bearing" — which is exactly why its absence on the other three is a defect, not a nit. `DataTable.d.ts` states the rule unconditionally ("the column takes the **full width** of the stacked card with its label above rather than beside it") and fences nothing; no specimen exercises the combination, because no teaching surface renders a stacked wrap cell with `onRowClick` at all (`marks-and-chips.card.html` passes no `onRowClick`; app-layout's Mobile() uses `RecordCard`, not `DataTable`). 2. The M01-34 empty case is taught three different ways, and two of them improvise past `NamedGap`. `templates/app-layout/app.jsx`: `empty={}`. But `components/data/marks-and-chips.card.html` — the @dsCard for this gap — uses `empty={No roles yet}`, and `components/data/DataTable.prompt.md` (a file they did not open, though they read DataTable.jsx and .d.ts) repeats the identical hand-rolled span verbatim in its "A cell that holds several chips" section. `ChipGroup.prompt.md` gives a third answer, `empty={null}`. That contradicts the system's own law: `NamedGap.jsx` — "Three scales of the same honesty, and nothing improvises between them" and "THE WORDS ARE READ, so they take --text-secondary" — and SKILL.md's "An absent value says what is missing… `NamedGap` in the value's own footprint". A table cell at `scale="cell"` is 13px/`--text-secondary` plus the hollow non-colour ring; the improvised span is 12px/`--text-tertiary` with no ring. I recomputed `--text-tertiary` #6B6E74: 5.11:1 on #FFFFFF (matches the token comment) and 4.94:1 on `--surface-alt` #FAFBFC, so this is not a contrast failure — it is a second treatment of an idea the system already ruled on, on the two surfaces a designer copies for F2-10. 3. Minor, but it undercuts "the template proves it at both sizes": app-layout's phone half is `marks={flagMarks(l)}` → `MarkRow`, which has no cap and no "+N" at all. The file says so itself ("on the card nothing collapses"), so it is deliberate — but it means the bounded-group behaviour is demonstrated at 1440 and not at 375 anywhere in the layout reference, and `readme.md:298`'s "The card *is* the table row — same fields, same order, same words" reads as more parity than exists. Only `marks-and-chips.card.html` shows the stacked form. Net: the component exists with the required API and the desktop cell half is real; the stacked half is conditional on a column falling into `rest`, and the canonical examples teach an improvised absence treatment. PARTIAL, not CLOSED.

gaps.component: Calendar/DatePicker reading month names, weekday names, field order and first-day-of-week from the market pack via useFormat(); DateSet and DocumentPreview on the same path; format.js resolveFirstDay reading the RAW pack
gaps.evidence:
THE COMPONENT. The two hardcoded arrays are gone. DatePicker.jsx now opens `import { useFormat } from "../data/MarketProvider.jsx";` and every one of the three market facts is read: `const startIdx = mkt.firstDayOfWeek % 7;` / `const offset = (first.getDay() - startIdx + 7) % 7;` (the first column), `const narrowDays = mkt.weekdayNames("narrow"); const longDays = mkt.weekdayNames("long");` (the day names), `{mkt.monthYear(view)}` in the header, `aria-label={`${mkt.date(d)}...`}` on every cell, and the field text `(value ? mkt.date(parse(value)) : "")`. `formatDate` survives only as `return (format || IN_FORMAT).date(d);` — the default pack, documented as such. There is no `firstDayOfWeek` prop on CalendarProps or DatePickerProps, and DatePicker.d.ts states why: "There is no `firstDayOfWeek` prop: the week start is a market fact, so it comes from the pack and a screen cannot disagree with it."

THE RAW-NOT-IN-MERGED CHECK — THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND IT PASSES. format.js computes `const firstDayOfWeek = resolveFirstDay(pack, p.locale);` — it passes the RAW `pack` argument, not the merged `p = { ...IN_PACK, ...pack }`, and resolveFirstDay's own comment names the trap: "IT READS THE RAW PACK, NOT THE MERGED ONE... a GB pack that says nothing about days must not inherit India's Sunday, it must get en-GB's Monday." I ran the real logic in node rather than accept it: `{locale:"en-GB",currency:"GBP"}` resolves to 1 and yields the column order `Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun`, while the same pack read through the IN-merged object returns 7 (India's Sunday). en-IN → 7 (`Sun Mon Tue...`), fr-FR → 1 (`lun. mar. mer...`), and a pack with no locale at all correctly inherits en-IN → 7. Grid arithmetic verified too: 1 Mar 2026 is a Sunday, so offset is 0 under the IN pack (column one) and 6 under a Monday pack (column seven). Field order is genuinely locale-driven: en-IN/en-GB "12 Mar 2026", en-US "Mar 12, 2026", fr-FR "12 mars 2026". weekdayNames returns names starting at firstDayOfWeek, and DateSet.weekdayOf applies the exact inverse mapping `long[(d.getDay() - startIdx + 7) % 7]`, so grid and list cannot disagree.

14A'S SECOND RESIDUE FIXED. DocumentPreview.jsx no longer passes a pre-formatted string through: `docDate = "2026-08-16"` rendered as `{mkt.date(docDate)}`, with `const amount = (v) => (typeof v === "number" ? mkt.money(v) : v);` and `const taxLabel = taxIdLabel || mkt.pack.taxIdLabel;`.

TEACHING SURFACES AGREE, INCLUDING THE GB CASE. DatePicker.prompt.md carries the worked example `<MarketProvider pack={{ locale: "en-GB", currency: "GBP", currencySymbol: "£" }}><Calendar month="2026-03-01" .../></MarketProvider>` commented "Monday first column, that pack's month names" — which I confirmed is what the code actually does. MarketProvider.prompt.md repeats it and states the resolution order: "A pack that doesn't say gets its locale's CLDR answer, with Monday as the last resort." readme.md L68: "**Currency, grouping, dates and clock are market-pack data, not content rules** (`F1` / `F3-20`)... **and a week that starts Sunday**... the **first day of the week**, which `Calendar` hardcoded as Monday until the pack supplied it." readme.md L121: "`Calendar`/`DatePicker` read all three from the pack and take no `firstDayOfWeek` prop."

THE OTHER LEGS OF THE GAP ALSO LANDED. Charts.jsx: `const fmt = format || mkt.number;` in BarChart, LineChart, DonutChart and FunnelChart, with `export const inr = (n) => IN_FORMAT.money(n)` kept only as an explicit IN shortcut. UsageMeter.jsx: `const mkt = useFormat(); const fmt = mkt.number;`. TimeField.d.ts: "What the user reads and types follows the active market pack's clock." NumberField.d.ts has `currency?: boolean` — "Display the amount in the active market's currency and grouping (F1 / F3-20)... The pack's symbol is a leading (or trailing) adornment inside the box" — which is the ENTERED half of the gap statement. A regex sweep of the whole compiled `_ds_bundle.js` finds `en-IN` surviving in exactly two non-comment places: `IN_PACK.locale` and nothing else, and zero `toLocaleString` call sites.
gaps.crossCutting:
Four things worth the parent's attention. None of them reopens a gap in my group, but two are neighbour contradictions of exactly the kind the method asks for.

1. BLOCK, TABS AND SEGMENTEDCONTROL ANSWER "A COUNT BESIDE A LABEL" DIFFERENTLY, AND THE DOCS CLAIM THEY DO NOT. Block.prompt.md, blocks.card.html and readme.md L119 all say Block's count is "the same idiom `Tabs` and `SegmentedControl` already use", and justify Block's behaviour with "clamping a reported number to '99+' would be a lie about it". Visually the claim holds — Block's COUNT_PILL and Tabs' COUNT are byte-identical (`height: 20, padding: "0 7px", borderRadius: "var(--r-pill)", fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 500, fontVariantNumeric: "tabular-nums"`, neutral-bg/neutral-text when inactive). Numerically they contradict each other in precisely the dimension the copy makes a principle: Tabs.jsx renders `{t.count > 99 ? "99+" : t.count}` and SegmentedControl.jsx renders `{o.count > 99 ? "99+" : o.count}` — both hardcode the clamp Block's own documentation calls a lie, and neither calls `useFormat()`, so neither groups. "Documents 1,240" in a Block is "99+" in a tab strip directly above it. The system's own instrument already demonstrates this: guidelines/touch-targets.card.html's appendix mounts `<SegmentedControl options={[{ value: "mine", label: "Mine", count: 8 }, { value: "all", label: "All", count: 214 }]} />`, which renders "All 99+". Either Tabs/SegmentedControl should take the pack and the opt-in `countMax`, or the three files claiming one idiom should stop claiming it.

2. A BLOCK'S COUNT DISAPPEARS WITHOUT A TITLE. In Block.jsx the header is gated on `const head = overline || title || meta || action || badge || shownCount;` but both `shownCount` and `badge` are rendered only inside the inner `{title && (...)}` branch. So `<Block overline="Documents" count={14} countLabel="documents" />` draws a header containing the overline and no count at all, and `<Block count={14} />` draws an empty header. Every shipped example passes a title and the gap specifies a *titled* container, so nothing is blocked from being drawn — but a screen author who leads with an overline loses the count silently rather than getting an error. One-line fix: hoist the count/badge row out of the `title` conditional.

3. THREE FILES NAME A FORMATTER THE COMPONENT DOES NOT CALL. DatePicker.jsx's header comment ("month and day names → mkt.monthNames() / mkt.weekdayNames()"), DatePicker.prompt.md ("`mkt.monthNames()` and `mkt.weekdayNames()`, not the two English arrays this file used to hold") and MarketProvider.prompt.md ("`f.monthNames()`, `f.weekdayNames()`") all state that Calendar's month names come from `monthNames()`. Calendar never calls it — the heading is `{mkt.monthYear(view)}`. A grep of the whole compiled `_ds_bundle.js` finds `monthNames` at exactly two sites: its definition in format.js and its entry in the returned object. It is a live, typed, documented, zero-caller API. The rendered behaviour is still correct (monthYear is equally locale-driven), so this is doc-only drift rather than a defect — but it is the kind of drift that makes the next reader believe a dead function is load-bearing.

4. TWO INDIA-BAKED RESIDUES THAT ARE CALLER DATA, NOT COMPONENT BEHAVIOUR. readme.md L5 still carries the sentence the original gap-6 audit quoted — "Content is Indian: ₹ in Indian format (₹4,52,471)" — under **Character**, while L68 rules "Currency, grouping, dates and clock are market-pack data, not content rules". L68 is unambiguous and explicitly supersedes, so I do not read this as a contradicting law, but the two sentences sit 60 lines apart with no cross-reference. Separately, all three templates hardcode pre-formatted money and date strings as row data (`value: "₹4,52,000"`, `when: "22 Jul"`, `when: "till 12 Aug"`) and pass them into a `numeric: true` DataTable column, and readme.md L306 calls templates/app-layout "**the layout standard**: ... Start here for any new screen — copy the arrangement, swap the content." No component bakes anything, so gap 6 stays closed — but the file 99 screens are told to copy demonstrates hand-formatted Indian figures rather than numbers through the pack.

I re-ran format.js's real resolveFirstDay/weekdayNames logic in node rather than trust the assertion: {locale:"en-GB"} -> firstDay 1 -> "Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun"; {locale:"en-IN"} -> 7 -> "Sun Mon Tue..."; fr-FR -> 1 -> "lun. mar. mer."; {} -> 7. The raw-vs-merged trap is real and passes: `const firstDayOfWeek = resolveFirstDay(pack, p.locale);` passes the raw `pack`, not `p = { ...IN_PACK, ...pack }`. DatePicker.jsx reads all three facts (`const startIdx = mkt.firstDayOfWeek % 7;`, `mkt.weekdayNames("narrow")`, `{mkt.monthYear(view)}`) and its .d.ts and .prompt.md agree, including the en-GB example. DocumentPreview's .d.ts and .prompt.md — which the claim never opened, and which the audit named for `gstin` and "pre-formatted in Indian grouping" — are also clean: `taxIdLabel?: string; /** ...defaults to the market pack ("GSTIN" here, "VAT number" elsewhere). */` and "Amounts are numbers, not pre-formatted strings." NumberField.jsx (the ENTERED half, .jsx never opened by the claim) really implements it: `const symbol = currency ? mkt.currencySymbol : null;` with `mkt.parseNumber`, and money-and-held-photos.card.html teaches it with a live non-IN pack (`pack={{id:"KE",...currencySymbol:"KSh"}}`). MoneySummary.jsx, StatCard.jsx, TimeField.jsx, UsageMeter.jsx all read useFormat().

WHAT REFUTES CLOSED: the claim certified the Charts leg from Charts.jsx alone. Charts.jsx is indeed fixed (`const fmt = format || mkt.number;` in all four charts), but ALL THREE of its teaching surfaces still teach the baked-IN form — the exact failure mode this audit exists to catch.

1. components/charts/Charts.d.ts — the API declaration, and a .d.ts that contradicts its .jsx. The strings "pack", "market", "MarketProvider" and "useFormat" appear NOWHERE in the file. It declares `format?: (n: number) => string;` on BarChart/LineChart/DonutChart/FunnelChart with no statement that omitting it yields the market pack, still documents the shortcut as an unqualified product fact — "/** ₹ in Indian grouping — ₹4,52,471. */ export function inr(n: number): string;" — and teaches the headline as a pre-formatted rupee string: "/** Headline figure above the plot, e.g. \"₹1,24,00,000\". */ value?: React.ReactNode;".

2. components/charts/charts.card.html — the @dsCard canonical example, never opened by the claim. It re-establishes the shortcut (`const inr = Charts.inr;`) and then BOTH money charts override the pack: `<LineChart ... value="₹94,20,000" ... format={inr}` and `<DonutChart ... centerValue="₹1.24 Cr" size={148} format={inr}`. No MarketProvider appears anywhere on the card. Only FunnelChart demonstrates the pack default; every chart that renders money re-bakes IN_FORMAT.money.

3. components/charts/Charts.prompt.md — carries the correct law ("**Number formatting comes from the market pack**, not from this file — pass `format` only to override it") and then contradicts it in its ONLY money worked example: `centerValue="₹1.24 Cr" format={inr}`.

Also a law contradicting a law in readme.md. L68 declares "**Currency, grouping, dates and clock are market-pack data, not content rules** (`F1` / `F3-20`)" — the line the claim quoted — while L7, which the claim did not read, still states it as a content rule: "Content is Indian: ₹ in Indian format (₹4,52,471), Indian names/cities, kWp system sizes, GST, DISCOM utilities." That is the register's own cited residue ("readme.md fixes it as a system fundamental") surviving one line-set away from its fix. Minor by comparison: UsageMeter.d.ts and .prompt.md never mention the pack at all (silent rather than contradicting), and AllocationMeter renders figures through a plain rounder `const nfmt = n => {...}` with no pack grouping (defensible — it is percentages).

PARTIAL, not CLOSED.

Four things worth the parent's attention. None of them reopens a gap in my group, but two are neighbour contradictions of exactly the kind the method asks for.

1. BLOCK, TABS AND SEGMENTEDCONTROL ANSWER "A COUNT BESIDE A LABEL" DIFFERENTLY, AND THE DOCS CLAIM THEY DO NOT. Block.prompt.md, blocks.card.html and readme.md L119 all say Block's count is "the same idiom `Tabs` and `SegmentedControl` already use", and justify Block's behaviour with "clamping a reported number to '99+' would be a lie about it". Visually the claim holds — Block's COUNT_PILL and Tabs' COUNT are byte-identical (`height: 20, padding: "0 7px", borderRadius: "var(--r-pill)", fontSize: 12, fontWeight: 500, fontVariantNumeric: "tabular-nums"`, neutral-bg/neutral-text when inactive). Numerically they contradict each other in precisely the dimension the copy makes a principle: Tabs.jsx renders `{t.count > 99 ? "99+" : t.count}` and SegmentedControl.jsx renders `{o.count > 99 ? "99+" : o.count}` — both hardcode the clamp Block's own documentation calls a lie, and neither calls `useFormat()`, so neither groups. "Documents 1,240" in a Block is "99+" in a tab strip directly above it. The system's own instrument already demonstrates this: guidelines/touch-targets.card.html's appendix mounts `<SegmentedControl options={[{ value: "mine", label: "Mine", count: 8 }, { value: "all", label: "All", count: 214 }]} />`, which renders "All 99+". Either Tabs/SegmentedControl should take the pack and the opt-in `countMax`, or the three files claiming one idiom should stop claiming it.

2. A BLOCK'S COUNT DISAPPEARS WITHOUT A TITLE. In Block.jsx the header is gated on `const head = overline || title || meta || action || badge || shownCount;` but both `shownCount` and `badge` are rendered only inside the inner `{title && (...)}` branch. So `<Block overline="Documents" count={14} countLabel="documents" />` draws a header containing the overline and no count at all, and `<Block count={14} />` draws an empty header. Every shipped example passes a title and the gap specifies a *titled* container, so nothing is blocked from being drawn — but a screen author who leads with an overline loses the count silently rather than getting an error. One-line fix: hoist the count/badge row out of the `title` conditional.

3. THREE FILES NAME A FORMATTER THE COMPONENT DOES NOT CALL. DatePicker.jsx's header comment ("month and day names → mkt.monthNames() / mkt.weekdayNames()"), DatePicker.prompt.md ("`mkt.monthNames()` and `mkt.weekdayNames()`, not the two English arrays this file used to hold") and MarketProvider.prompt.md ("`f.monthNames()`, `f.weekdayNames()`") all state that Calendar's month names come from `monthNames()`. Calendar never calls it — the heading is `{mkt.monthYear(view)}`. A grep of the whole compiled `_ds_bundle.js` finds `monthNames` at exactly two sites: its definition in format.js and its entry in the returned object. It is a live, typed, documented, zero-caller API. The rendered behaviour is still correct (monthYear is equally locale-driven), so this is doc-only drift rather than a defect — but it is the kind of drift that makes the next reader believe a dead function is load-bearing.

4. TWO INDIA-BAKED RESIDUES THAT ARE CALLER DATA, NOT COMPONENT BEHAVIOUR. readme.md L5 still carries the sentence the original gap-6 audit quoted — "Content is Indian: ₹ in Indian format (₹4,52,471)" — under **Character**, while L68 rules "Currency, grouping, dates and clock are market-pack data, not content rules". L68 is unambiguous and explicitly supersedes, so I do not read this as a contradicting law, but the two sentences sit 60 lines apart with no cross-reference. Separately, all three templates hardcode pre-formatted money and date strings as row data (`value: "₹4,52,000"`, `when: "22 Jul"`, `when: "till 12 Aug"`) and pass them into a `numeric: true` DataTable column, and readme.md L306 calls templates/app-layout "**the layout standard**: ... Start here for any new screen — copy the arrangement, swap the content." No component bakes anything, so gap 6 stays closed — but the file 99 screens are told to copy demonstrates hand-formatted Indian figures rather than numbers through the pack.

The component-level fix landed and its per-component teaching surfaces agree, but the readme law that carries gap 10 teaches an enforcement guarantee the code does not provide, and the claim's sixth-site sweep is not a valid method.

PRESENT (quoted from the live project c8aa4326-21bf-453a-8d11-749cc81dee12):
- Menu.jsx default trigger: `style={{ width: 44, height: 44, display: "grid", placeItems: "center", ... }}`; Menu.d.ts: `/** Custom trigger element. Defaults to a 44x44 overflow button. */`; Menu.prompt.md: "// The default trigger is already 44x44". Residue 1 of round 14A is genuinely closed.
- Banner.jsx BannerAction: `style={{ minHeight: 44, minWidth: 44, margin: "-6px 0", padding: "0 2px", ... }}` wrapping `<span style={{ ... height: 32, padding: "0 12px", borderRadius: "var(--r-pill)", boxShadow: "var(--e1)", ... }}>`. That is legal shape #2 of the four the readme lists (44 box + smaller pill + negative margin), and the hit box is 44 because minHeight sits on the border box. Banner.d.ts ("**44px target, 32px pill.**"), Banner.prompt.md ("the button is **44px tall** while the pill you see stays **32px**") and banner.card.html ("The action's target is 44, the pill you see is 32", and every worked example uses <BannerAction> rather than a hand-rolled pill) all agree. Residue 2 is closed.
- All four original sites re-read in the live .jsx: Kanban.jsx MoveControls `style={{ width: 44, height: 44, ... }}`; DataTable.jsx SelectionBar `style={{ width: 44, height: 44, marginLeft: -10, ... }}` and Pagination btn `style={{ width: 44, height: 44, ... }}`; Menu trigger 44x44; Banner dismiss `style={{ width: 44, height: 44, margin: "-12px -12px -12px 0", ... }}`.
- Neighbour teaching surfaces the claim did not open also agree: Kanban.d.ts ("always-visible 44px move buttons") and Kanban.prompt.md ("The always-visible 44px move buttons are the keyboard and touch route"); SKILL.md ("Every interactive element is >=44x44, measured on the hit box. Four legal shapes ... The single exception is a pointer-only affordance inside a `<table>` data row"). All three templates carry `const size = stacked ? 44 : 32;`, including mobile-field-app's unrendered Desktop().

MISSING:
1. readme.md's own enforcement law is false. Line 30: "How the floor is enforced, so this is the last sweep. `guidelines/touch-targets.card.html` measures it in the browser on every load: it opens **every component specimen card** and the three templates in iframes at 1280px and 390px". Line 87: "it re-measures **every interactive element in every card and template** on load". SKILL.md repeats it: "re-measures the whole system on load". The instrument's actual CARDS array holds 48 component cards plus `./field-mode.card.html`; the project contains 59 component `.card.html` files. Eleven are in neither CARDS nor PHONE and are therefore never measured at any width: charts/pin-placement, data/banded-figure, data/checklist, data/derivation, data/money-summary, feedback/disclosure, feedback/generate-gate, feedback/pending-and-progress, forms/money-and-held-photos, print/drawing-sheet, print/paged-document. Two of those are phone-first surfaces this gap's own PRD rows reach (MS1-16/SCR-MS-04 touch pin placement; M11-37's held-photo capture queue). The claim repeats the false version verbatim — "re-measures every card and all three templates".
2. The instrument encodes a wider exception than the written one. touch-targets.card.html: `const inRow = !!el.closest("tr");` then `const verdict = kbOnly ? "n/a" : (w >= MIN - 0.6 && h >= MIN - 0.6) ? "pass" : inRow ? "exception" : "FAIL";`. readme.md binds the exception to three conditions — "only in the `<table>` row, only pointer-only, only where the act repeats at full size elsewhere". As coded, any sub-44 control anywhere in a table row is printed as "in-row exception" and can never print FAIL, so the instrument cannot detect the exact failure the original audit named ("The escape clause also fails on its own terms at SCR-M02-02 ... so there is no full-size repeat to fall back on").
3. The claim's sixth-site evidence does not hold. A regex over numeric height/width/minHeight/minWidth literals near a button cannot see a size held in a constant, and the system's own reference component proves it: FilterBar.jsx declares `const TOUCH = 44; const PILL = { scope: 36, chip: 34, sort: 32, filters: 36 };` and applies them as `height: PILL.scope`. Four sub-44 pills in one file, none spelled as a numeric `height:` literal — yet the claim reports "exactly two hits" across the whole bundle and names "FilterBar's documented 34px pill" as one of them, which is not reproducible. The templates' `const size = stacked ? 44 : 32;` is invisible to the same regex. I re-ran the sweep on the compiled bundle myself (get_file truncates it at 261,404 chars, ~29 of 100 modules, so it is not a whole-system sweep either) and then hand-read four of the unmeasured components — Checklist.jsx (tick button `minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44`), MapSurface.jsx (Ctrl and Marker `width: 44, height: 44`), FindingList.jsx (`pillBase` `minHeight: 44`), OperationProgress.jsx (cancel/retry `minHeight: 44`) — all compliant. So no sixth site is proven, but none is ruled out either: the method the claim relied on cannot rule one out, and the instrument the readme says makes this "the last sweep" skips eleven cards.

Net: the capability the gap required exists at all five sites with agreeing per-component teaching surfaces; the law in readme.md and SKILL.md that governs it, and the instrument it points at, still teach a coverage guarantee that is not true. PARTIAL, not CLOSED.

gaps.refuteWhy:
MOSTLY CONFIRMED, NOT FULLY CLOSED. The capability is real and I could not break it: Block.d.ts declares `count?: number` / `countMax?: number` / `countLabel?: string` and re-scopes `badge` ("**A count goes in `count`, not here.**"); Block.jsx implements it with its own COUNT_PILL (`background:"var(--neutral-bg)", color:"var(--neutral-text)", fontSize:12, fontVariantNumeric:"tabular-nums"`), `const n = typeof count === "number" && count > 0 ? count : null;` and `const shownCount = n === null ? null : countMax != null && n > countMax ? `${countMax}+` : mkt.number(n,{maximumFractionDigits:0});`. Checks the claimant did not run, all of which pass: (a) _ds_bundle.js — the file every .card.html and template loads — carries the SAME count logic, not a stale Block, so the card demo is live rather than aspirational; (b) grouping is not gated on a provider: MarketProvider.jsx does `React.createContext(IN_FORMAT)` and format.js exports `IN_FORMAT = createFormat(IN_PACK)`, so `count={1240}` renders "1,240" with no MarketProvider anywhere; (c) the "not CountBadge" rationale holds in the .jsx, not only the .d.ts — AppShell.jsx: `tone = "danger"`, `const words = n === null ? `Unread ${label}` : `${n} unread ${label}`;`, `boxShadow:"0 0 0 2px var(--surface)"`; (d) recomputed contrast: --neutral-text #585B60 on --neutral-bg #F0F1F3 = 6.03:1 (base) and #3A3D42 on #F0F1F3 = 9.65:1 in field mode — both clear 4.5; 12px equals the `--fs-caption` floor readme L46 sets for counters; (e) no template teaches the old form — none of the three app.jsx files uses Block at all, in either half. TWO THINGS BLOCK A FULL CLOSE. 1. DEFECT — the count is silently dropped unless `title` is set, and the file contradicts itself about it. Block.jsx computes `const head = overline || title || meta || action || badge || shownCount;` — treating a count as sufficient reason to draw the header — but the pill renders INSIDE the title branch: `{title && (

{title}

{shownCount && (…)}{badge}
)}`. `title?: string` is optional in the .d.ts. So `` — an overline-only today-block, exactly the SCR-M07-01 / M13-10 shape the gap was written for — renders the overline, an otherwise-empty header row, and no numeral, with no warning. Reproduced byte-identically in the shipped bundle. `badge` has the same gate. 2. TEACHING SURFACE ASSERTS A CROSS-COMPONENT FACT THAT IS FALSE, AND THE SYSTEM NOW RENDERS ONE NUMERAL THREE WAYS. Block.jsx, Block.prompt.md ("the same idiom `Tabs` and `SegmentedControl` already use") and blocks.card.html ("a tabular numeral in a neutral pill, the same idiom `Tabs` and `SegmentedControl` use") all cite the neighbours as precedent. SegmentedControl.jsx renders its count with NO pill — `{o.count > 99 ? "99+" : o.count}`, its comment saying "no pill — the segment is already a pill". And both neighbours hardcode `count > 99 ? "99+" : count` with no call to useFormat and no way to disable the clamp, so `1240` is "1,240" in a Block and "99+" in a Tab — the two components Block's docs offer as the same idiom do exactly what Block's own law calls a lie ("clamping a total lies" / "a total groups instead of clamping"). Related, one component over: Accordion.d.ts still documents the other section header's count as free text — `meta?: string` "a count, a status ("12 items")" — echoed by readme L169 ("`meta` is a count or a status"), so a section's "how many" has two contradicting answers in the system a screen author will meet. Minor, pre-existing, not caused here: COUNT_PILL uses `fontWeight: 500` against readme L46 ("500 allowed for buttons, tabs and table headers only"), but Chip, Badge and StatusChip already do the same. Also noted for the wider gap-12 picture: SKILL.md — the file a screen author reads first — names Block only as "a `Block`'s `empty` state for a section" and never as the composition unit, and templates/app-layout (which SKILL.md says to start every screen from) contains no Block or BlockGrid at all.
