gaps.crossCutting:
TWO NEIGHBOUR-LEVEL TENSIONS, BOTH DOC-LEVEL, NEITHER BLOCKING.

1. "One renderer" for the fourth state is stated more absolutely than the system actually holds. readme.md line 130 says "`UnavailableNote` — **the fourth state's one renderer.**" and UnavailableNote.jsx's own header calls itself "THE FOURTH STATE, and the one renderer of it", with the design claim "Neutral by construction: `--neutral-bg` mark, `--text-secondary` words, no warning tint". AudioPlayer bypasses it whenever a reason is known: `const REASONS = { "consent-declined": { icon: "mic-off", bg: "var(--neutral-bg)", ... }, "purged-retention": { icon: "clock", bg: "var(--info-bg)", fg: "var(--info)", ... } }` rendered into its own block (`background: s.bg, color: s.fg`) — so one of the two unavailable sentences in the system carries an **info tint**, which is a second visual treatment of a state whose whole claim is that it is untinted. This is declared rather than drifted (UnavailableNote.d.ts: "Where a component has two unavailable *reasons* that must not look alike ... the **state** is shared and the **reason** stays a local prop with its own words and glyph", and readme law 1 repeats it), so I did not downgrade gap 13 for it. But "one renderer" and "no tint" are both now approximations, and the next component with two unavailable reasons will read line 130, not law 1's qualifier. Worth tightening the line to "one renderer, and one declared exception".

2. Every surface is typed with the full five-member `SurfaceState` but not every surface handles all five. AudioPlayer.d.ts declares `state?: SurfaceState` yet AudioPlayer.jsx branches only on `loading`, `error` and `unavailable` — `state="empty"` falls through to the ready path and renders a live transport with no `src`, i.e. a dead play button and a `--:--` scrubber. CompareGrid and DataTable defend against this by folding empty into a data check (`if (state === "empty" || options.length === 0 || attributes.length === 0)`, `if (state === "empty" || rows.length === 0)`); AudioPlayer has no equivalent. A shared union is only as strong as its least complete implementor, and `isBlockedState` — exported precisely to answer "must this surface not draw content" — is not consulted by any of the components I read. Low impact for my four gaps (no screen has a reason to pass `empty` to a call recording), but it is the shape of a future private-fifth-state regression.

3. Minor wording drift on the actor vocabulary's host count: ActivityStream.prompt.md says "One vocabulary, two hosts: `entry.actorClass` here, `NextAction.origin` there" while ActorClass.jsx, NextAction.prompt.md and readme.md line 109 all say three hosts (ActivityStream, NextAction, Transcript). Doc-only; the prompt does describe Transcript correctly two paragraphs later.
gaps.refuteWhy:
Much of the claim survives: UnavailableNote + SurfaceState exist; Card.jsx genuinely implements all four non-ready branches (`state === "loading" ? <Shimmer/>x3 : state === "error" ? <CardMessage tone="warning".../> : state === "unavailable" ? <UnavailableNote .../> : state === "empty" ? <CardMessage .../> : children`); DataTable.d.ts, Timeline.d.ts, StatCard.d.ts, Card.d.ts all `import { SurfaceState } from "../feedback/UnavailableNote"`; Kanban.d.ts carries all five members. MapSurface.prompt.md and AudioPlayer.prompt.md — two teaching surfaces the claimant never opened — both correctly teach the new form ("`tiles-unavailable` is gone", "the old `status` union ... folded into the system's"). Those threads are clean.

But three things break the CLOSED verdict.

1. THE BUG — `error` and `unavailable` are unreachable on UsageMeter, the component the gap was written for. UsageMeter.jsx orders its guards:
  `const resolved = typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value);`
  `if (state === "loading" || !resolved) { return (<section ... role="status" aria-label={`${label}..., not resolved yet`}> ... {loadingNote} ...) }`
  ...then `/* RULE 3 */ if (state === "error")` and `if (state === "unavailable")` BELOW it.
UsageMeter.d.ts declares `value?: number` — optional — and documents `errorMessage` as "`error`'s sentence. It never quotes a figure", `onRetry` as "Draws the retry under `error`", and `unavailable` as "this meter does not apply to this plan. No bar, no figure, no retry." In both states there is definitionally no value: the default errorMessage is "Couldn't read this period's usage. Nothing is shown until it resolves." So the documented, natural call — `<UsageMeter label="AI designs" state="error" onRetry={r} />` or `state="unavailable"` with no `value` — hits `!resolved` first and silently renders the LOADING shimmer, announcing "not resolved yet" via `role="status"`, with the retry button unreachable. This is exactly the hunt target "a capability reachable only via a prop the default does not set": `value` has no default, and only a dummy finite `value` (e.g. `value={0}`) reaches the error/unavailable branches. SCR-M12-04's ruled error state — "this screen may only ever show the enforced/billed numbers" — therefore cannot be drawn as documented. The claimant quoted both guards separately and never noticed the first swallows the other two.

2. UsageMeter never joined the shared vocabulary, while three teaching surfaces say it did. UsageMeter.d.ts does NOT import SurfaceState; it declares its own `export type UsageState = "ok" | "overage-accruing" | "tracked-seats-accruing" | "cap-reached-grace" | "creations-paused" | "loading" | "error" | "unavailable"` — no `ready`, no `empty` — and UsageMeter.jsx defaults `state = "ok"`. The claimant quoted the signature as `export function UsageMeter({ label, value, limit = null, unit, ... })`, eliding `state = "ok"`. Against that: readme.md law 1 — "`ready | loading | empty | error | unavailable` — one vocabulary, on every surface, with `SurfaceState` and one renderer (`UnavailableNote`) to keep it that way"; readme.md's UnavailableNote entry — "Also exports `SurfaceState`, the five-member vocabulary every surface takes"; and UnavailableNote.prompt.md — "The state is on every surface that has a `state` — `Block`, `Card`, `StatCard`, ... `UsageMeter` — so nobody spells it privately again." A screen author following law 1 writes `state="ready"` and silently gets the `ok` fallback (`STATE_TONE["ready"]` is undefined → `fill` falls back to `var(--accent)`); `state="empty"` falls through to the full metered render.

3. The two containers the gap names by name still teach the pre-gap API. Card.prompt.md — Card's canonical example — never mentions `state`; it documents only "`density` ... `interactive` adds hover lift; `selected` adds the accent ring" and its one example is `<Card interactive>` with children. StatCard.prompt.md runs ~10 examples and not one uses `state`; it references the word only in passing ("a different statement from `state="empty"`"). The gap's own text is "Card and StatCard have none" and law 1 closes on "`Card` and `StatCard` ... had no `state` at all until they were given one" — but whoever opens either prompt.md to copy the component still sees the happy path only. Neither file is in the claimant's read list.

ACTOR IS A CLASS, NOT A FREE STRING. Order is newest-first by default (`order = "newest"` → `sorted.reverse()`), and the sort runs before every early return with the comment `/* Sorted before any early return, and deliberately not memoised: a hook after a conditional return changes the hook order between states */`. TIMELINE IS NOT THE SAME COMPONENT AND SAYS SO. Timeline.d.ts, unchanged in job: "**This is a sequence, not a stream.** An append-only activity log — 13+ kinds, four actor classes, hundreds of entries, every one of them `done` — is `ActivityStream`: the rail would light everything and say nothing ... `SCR-M08-02` needs both on one screen, one directly beneath the other", and its `actor` prop is now documented as the limit rather than the feature: "**A free string, and that is the limit of what this component claims:** it cannot distinguish a person from the agent, the system or the customer ... gaps.refuteWhy:
Most of the claim survives — I confirmed the entry shape, the 16-kind open registry, ActorClass's four-class vocabulary, the pure filter helpers, day grouping and the count line by reading ActivityStream.jsx/.d.ts/.prompt.md, ActorClass.jsx/.d.ts, activity-stream.card.html (registered in _ds_manifest.json), task-attribution.card.html, Timeline.jsx/.d.ts/.prompt.md, data-composites.card.html, readme.md lines 109-110, FilterPanel.d.ts (`kind: "facet"` with `counts`/`hint` is a real dimension), MarketProvider.d.ts (`time: (hhmm: string)` matches the call) and all three templates. Three things the claim did not check refute CLOSED.

1) THE SERVER-PAGING PATH IS DEAD, AND IT IS THE ONE THE REGISTER NAMES. The register binds SCR-M12-02: "a dunning history that can be long — the ladder runs day 0/2/4/6/7 then post-halt weekly x 4 then monthly, indefinitely". d.ts sells the answer — `/** For server paging: there are more entries than were handed over. */ hasMore?: boolean;` — and .prompt.md teaches it: "hand the window to the server: pass `hasMore` and `onLoadMore` and the same button pages instead of slicing." But ActivityStream.jsx line 2 of the body is `React.useEffect(() => { setShown(visibleCount); }, [visibleCount, entries.length]);`. Traced: with 25 entries + `hasMore`, `localMore = sorted.length > visible.length` is false, so `showMore()` correctly calls `onLoadMore()`; the parent appends page 2, `entries.length` goes 25→50, the effect fires and resets `shown` to 25, and `const visible = sorted.slice(0, shown)` renders the SAME newest 25. Nothing on screen changes. The second click then takes the `localMore` branch and slices locally instead of calling the server again. The claim quoted `showMore` in isolation and it is correct in isolation; the reset effect defeats it. The effect exists to re-window when a filter narrows the list — a real need — but it was not reconciled with paging, and no teaching surface tells a caller to raise `visibleCount` instead.

2) A TEACHING SURFACE STILL TEACHES THE OLD FORM — the register's own "Where: Timeline — a step sequence, not a stream". Timeline.prompt.md's FIRST LINE, the one-line summary a screen author reads to pick a component, is still: "A sequence of steps: customer progress page, lead detail, project stages, **field activity log**." Timeline.jsx's header says the opposite in capitals — "IT IS A SEQUENCE, NOT A STREAM, and the field activity log is no longer one of its jobs" — and the same prompt.md contradicts itself four paragraphs down: "**A field activity log is not this component.**" The claim listed Timeline.d.ts among the files it read and never opened Timeline.prompt.md or Timeline.jsx.

3) AN UNMEASURED NUMBER, RECOMPUTED FROM tokens/colors.css. The kind mark is `background: color-mix(in srgb, ${tone} 6%, white)` with `color: tone` on the `<Glyph>`. readme.md: "Where a mark carries meaning on a tint — a `StatusChip` dot, an attendance marker, a provenance tier — it uses the `-text` partner too, since the plain token misses even the 3:1 non-text floor there." Computed glyph-on-its-own-tint: `--accent` #5A4BFF 4.96:1, `--danger` #E5484D 3.62:1, `--info` #3B82F6 3.44:1, `--success` #159A5B 3.38:1 — and `--warning` #E9A23B on #FEF9F3 = **2.07:1**, under WCAG's 3:1 non-text floor. `--warning` is the tone for `task` AND `dunning` — `dunning` being one of the two kinds this build added for SCR-M12-02. Timeline avoids this on the same idea by filling the node with the token and drawing the tick in `--text-inverse`; ActivityStream introduced a second, weaker treatment of "a glyph on a 6% tint of its own token" and no `-text` partner anywhere in the file.

gaps.component: CompareGrid — one table with a pinned attribute column and a horizontally-scrolling option axis, plus a named boundary to readme law 4's no-horizontal-scroll prohibition
gaps.evidence:
THE RULING THE GAP ASKED FOR EXISTS, AND IT IS IN THE LAW ITSELF. readme.md law 4 still states the prohibition — "There is no horizontally-scrolling table in this system" — and then carries the boundary in its own paragraph: "A **comparison transposes both axes**: the record is the *column* and the attribute is the *row* ... The harm the prohibition names cannot occur, and the prohibition's own remedy would *be* the harm ... So `CompareGrid` is **not an exception to this law; it is outside its subject**. The boundary that keeps it there: it is the **one** component in the system with a horizontal scroller, it scrolls its **option** axis only, its attribute axis is complete at every width, and **it is never used for records** — a list of leads is a `DataTable` and stacks." The same reasoning is written into CompareGrid.jsx's header block and repeated in CompareGrid.d.ts and CompareGrid.prompt.md, so no screen can borrow the reading to turn a records table sideways.

ALIGNMENT IS STRUCTURAL, WHICH IS THE HARD REQUIREMENT. One table, not N cards: `<table ... style={{ borderCollapse: "collapse", tableLayout: "fixed", width: "max-content", minWidth: "100%" }}>` with the attribute cell pinned — `const stickyCell = (zebra, extra = {}) => ({ position: "sticky", left: 0, zIndex: 2, width: labelWidth, minWidth: labelWidth, maxWidth: labelWidth, ... })` applied to `<th scope="row" style={stickyCell(zebra, ...)}>` — and the option headers as `<th key={o.key} scope="col" style={{ ..., scrollSnapAlign: "start", ... }}>` inside `scrollSnapType: "x mandatory", scrollPaddingLeft: labelWidth`. So a swipe lands a whole option against the labels, and `th scope="row"`/`scope="col"` give the screen-reader announcement the docstring claims.

IT NEVER STACKS AND IS OPERABLE WITHOUT TOUCH. There is no `stackBelow` prop in the signature at all. The option axis takes arrow keys — `onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === "ArrowRight") { e.preventDefault(); nudge(1); } else if (e.key === "ArrowLeft") { e.preventDefault(); nudge(-1); } }}` — plus real 44px controls: `<button type="button" aria-label="Previous option" onClick={() => nudge(-1)} disabled={pos.first <= 1} style={{ width: 44, height: 44, ... }}>`.

2–N: the code does not cap N (`options.map(...)` throughout; `bestKeys` loops all options), and SCR-MS-07's eleven rows and SCR-M12-03's plan chooser are both demonstrated in compare-grid.card.html.
gaps.stillMissing:
THE ONE MEASURABLE CLAIM ABOUT 375px IS FALSE, AND THE COMPONENT'S OWN CODE CONTRADICTS IT.

CompareGrid.d.ts, on `columnWidth`: "Option column width. **Default 196 — two columns plus the pinned labels fit a 375px screen.**" With `labelWidth` defaulting to 128, two option columns plus the pinned label column require 128 + 196 + 196 = **520px**. On a 375px viewport the visible option track is 375 − 128 = 247px, which is 1.26 columns. The claim is wrong by 145px.

compare-grid.card.html repeats it under the panel that is supposed to prove it. That panel renders `<CompareGrid caption="Compare variants" attributes={ATTRS} options={OPTS} selectedKey={chosen} onSelect={setChosen} columnWidth={168} labelWidth={112} ... />` inside `.phone{width:375px;padding:16px;box-sizing:border-box}` — an inner width of 343px — and captions it: "Two option columns and the pinned labels fit 375px; a swipe snaps the next whole variant against the labels." Two columns there need 112 + 168 + 168 = **448px** against 343px available. Off by 105px.

The component's own measurement disagrees with its caption on the same page. CompareGrid.jsx: `const track = Math.max(1, el.clientWidth - labelWidth); const per = Math.max(1, Math.round(track / columnWidth)); ... setPos({ scrollable: ..., first, last: Math.min(options.length, first + per - 1) });` — at 343px with labelWidth 112 and columnWidth 168, `track` = 231 and `per` = Math.round(1.375) = **1**. The readout rendered directly beneath that phone frame is `` `Showing ${pos.first === pos.last ? pos.first : ...} of ${options.length} — swipe or use the arrows` `` → "Showing 1 of 4", sitting immediately above a note claiming two fit. A screen author sizing SCR-MS-14 or SCR-M12-03 against the documented default will design a two-up phone comparison the defaults cannot deliver; to actually fit two at 375px, `columnWidth` has to drop to roughly 115.

Secondary: the gap asks for **2–N** whole options, and every doc surface caps it at 2–4 ("The columns — 2 to 4 options, and the snap rendering holds four" in CompareGrid.d.ts; "Compare 2–4 options" in the prompt and the @dsCard subtitle; "2–4 options compared attribute by attribute" in readme.md line 111). The code imposes no cap, so this is only a documentation ceiling — but SCR-MS-07's candidate set is not bounded at four by MS4-30, and a screen author reading the docs will believe it is.
gaps.crossCutting:
TWO NEIGHBOUR-LEVEL TENSIONS, BOTH DOC-LEVEL, NEITHER BLOCKING.

1. "One renderer" for the fourth state is stated more absolutely than the system actually holds. readme.md line 130 says "`UnavailableNote` — **the fourth state's one renderer.**" and UnavailableNote.jsx's own header calls itself "THE FOURTH STATE, and the one renderer of it", with the design claim "Neutral by construction: `--neutral-bg` mark, `--text-secondary` words, no warning tint". AudioPlayer bypasses it whenever a reason is known: `const REASONS = { "consent-declined": { icon: "mic-off", bg: "var(--neutral-bg)", ... }, "purged-retention": { icon: "clock", bg: "var(--info-bg)", fg: "var(--info)", ... } }` rendered into its own block (`background: s.bg, color: s.fg`) — so one of the two unavailable sentences in the system carries an **info tint**, which is a second visual treatment of a state whose whole claim is that it is untinted. This is declared rather than drifted (UnavailableNote.d.ts: "Where a component has two unavailable *reasons* that must not look alike ... the **state** is shared and the **reason** stays a local prop with its own words and glyph", and readme law 1 repeats it), so I did not downgrade gap 13 for it. But "one renderer" and "no tint" are both now approximations, and the next component with two unavailable reasons will read line 130, not law 1's qualifier. Worth tightening the line to "one renderer, and one declared exception".

2. Every surface is typed with the full five-member `SurfaceState` but not every surface handles all five. AudioPlayer.d.ts declares `state?: SurfaceState` yet AudioPlayer.jsx branches only on `loading`, `error` and `unavailable` — `state="empty"` falls through to the ready path and renders a live transport with no `src`, i.e. a dead play button and a `--:--` scrubber. CompareGrid and DataTable defend against this by folding empty into a data check (`if (state === "empty" || options.length === 0 || attributes.length === 0)`, `if (state === "empty" || rows.length === 0)`); AudioPlayer has no equivalent. A shared union is only as strong as its least complete implementor, and `isBlockedState` — exported precisely to answer "must this surface not draw content" — is not consulted by any of the components I read. Low impact for my four gaps (no screen has a reason to pass `empty` to a call recording), but it is the shape of a future private-fifth-state regression.

3. Minor wording drift on the actor vocabulary's host count: ActivityStream.prompt.md says "One vocabulary, two hosts: `entry.actorClass` here, `NextAction.origin` there" while ActorClass.jsx, NextAction.prompt.md and readme.md line 109 all say three hosts (ActivityStream, NextAction, Transcript). Doc-only; the prompt does describe Transcript correctly two paragraphs later.

gaps.component: ActionReason (precondition, control stays) + ScopeNote (permission, act absent) + ComplianceFloor (statute, act absent for everyone) — with `disabledReason` wired into all five hosts the audit named
gaps.evidence:
BOTH HALVES EXIST, IN CODE NOT JUST DOCS. Precondition half — ActionReason.jsx: `export function ActionReason({ reason, id, size = 12, align = "left", style = {} })` rendering `color: "var(--text-secondary)"` with a barred-circle glyph, plus the adapter `export function renderActionReason(spec, extra = {})`. Permission half — ScopeNote.jsx: `export function ScopeNote({ holder, acts, title, message, action, variant = "line", align = "left", size = 13, style = {} })` composing `const line = title || (holder ? (phrase ? `Only ${holder} can ${phrase}.` : ...))`, i.e. the act is absent and the screen names whose it is (M12-56 / SCR-M11-02). A third answer, ComplianceFloor, is argued for the statute case in readme.md law 9.

ALL FIVE `disabled` FLAGS THE AUDIT LISTED NOW CARRY A REASON SLOT, in .jsx AND .d.ts: Button (`disabledReason?: React.ReactNode | ActionReasonSpec`), IconButton (same), Menu's `MenuItem.disabledReason`, Select's `SelectOption.disabledReason`, OptionCardGroup's `OptionCardItem.disabledReason`.

THE MECHANICAL RULING (aria-disabled, stays focusable) IS REAL IN FOUR OF THE FIVE. Button.jsx: `const stated = disabled && !!disabledReason;` then `disabled={disabled && !stated} aria-disabled={disabled || undefined} aria-describedby={stated ? autoId : undefined}` with `onClick={(e) => { if (disabled) { e.preventDefault(); return; } ... }}`. IconButton.jsx is identical. Menu.jsx keeps such an item in the roving walk: `const enabled = items.map((it, i) => ({ it, i })).filter(({ it }) => !it.separator && (!it.disabled || !!it.disabledReason));` with `disabled={it.disabled && !reason} aria-disabled={it.disabled || undefined}`. OptionCardGroup.jsx: `while (options[t].disabled && !options[t].disabledReason && guard++ < options.length) t = ...` and `disabled={off && !reason} aria-disabled={off || undefined}`.

LAW AND SPEC CARD AGREE. readme.md law 9: "A control given a `disabledReason` is therefore `aria-disabled` and **stays focusable** with activation suppressed — and in `Menu` and `OptionCardGroup` it stays in the arrow-key walk, because a skipped item is one whose reason a keyboard user can never hear." SKILL.md: "A control with a stated reason is `aria-disabled` and stays focusable, or the sentence is announced to nobody." reason-and-scope.card.html renders Button, IconButton, Select, Menu and OptionCardGroup specimens with real reasons and states the same ruling.

MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED (computed from tokens/colors.css): --text-secondary #54565B on --surface #FFFFFF = 7.34:1, on --canvas #F6F7F9 = 6.85:1, on --canvas-sunken #EEF0F3 = 6.43:1 — the "never --text-disabled" rule holds and the reason line is readable everywhere it can land. The glyph in --text-tertiary #6B6E74 is 5.11 / 4.77, past the 3:1 non-text floor. Type floor enforced in code: `fontSize: Math.max(12, size)`. Hit box: Button/IconButton keep `minHeight: 44` / `minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44` with the reason added as a second row, so the column does not shrink the target.
gaps.stillMissing:
1) SELECT — the one host whose PRD row is verbatim (MS2-21 "disabled options explain WHY inline") — implements the reason but NOT the announcement half of the ruling. Select.jsx puts `role="combobox"` on the trigger with `aria-expanded={open} aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-controls={autoId + "-list"}` and NO `aria-activedescendant`; the options are `<li key={o.value} role="option" aria-selected={sel} aria-disabled={o.disabled || undefined} ...>` with NO `id`. Select.jsx asserts the opposite in its own header: "The row keeps its aria-disabled, and the reason is real text inside the option, so a screen reader reads both." That is the exact failure mode law 9 exists to prevent ("the sentence would exist for everyone except the keyboard user who most needs it"), reproduced one component over from where it was fixed.

2) FOUR OF THE FIVE HOSTS' .prompt.md FILES STILL TEACH THE PRE-GAP FORM. Button.prompt.md never mentions the slot and its prop list closes with the old shape: "Props: `loading` (spinner, fixed width), `disabled`, `icon`/`iconRight`, `fullWidth`." IconButton.prompt.md: no mention of `disabledReason` at all. Menu.prompt.md: no mention at all (it documents `selection`, `marks`, `meta`, `destructive`, `separator`, and stops). Select.prompt.md is the worst of the four — its canonical example smuggles the reason into the label, the one thing Select.d.ts forbids ("Never a tooltip (a touch user never opens one) and never folded into the label"): `{ value: "rahul", label: "Rahul Patil (on leave)", disabled: true }`. OptionCardGroup.prompt.md shows `{ value: "ground", title: "Ground mount", description: "Needs a civil foundation and 1.5× the panel area.", price: "₹1,12,000", disabled: true }` — a bare disabled option, no reason — and names `disabledReason` only in a closing negative ("**Not `option.disabledReason`**, which says why one option cannot be chosen"), so a reader meets the prop without ever seeing it used.

3) forms.card.html, the general Forms spec card, still shows `<Button variant="primary" disabled>Disabled</Button>` as the canonical disabled specimen. Legal under law 9 ("A `disabled` with no reason keeps the native attribute"), but combined with (2) the whole of a drawing agent's Button-local reading teaches the bare grey control.
gaps.crossCutting:
Four things surfaced that cross component boundaries.

1. TWO "PICK ONE FROM A POPUP LIST" COMPONENTS ANSWER GAP 37's MECHANICAL RULING DIFFERENTLY, AND ONLY ONE IS RIGHT. Menu.jsx moves real DOM focus onto the item (`ref={(el) => (itemRefs.current[i] = el)}`, `tabIndex={i === active ? 0 : -1}`, `React.useEffect(() => { if (open && itemRefs.current[active]) itemRefs.current[active].focus(); }, [open, active])`) and deliberately keeps a reasoned item in the walk. Whichever of the eleven screens uses a Select rather than a Menu gets the pre-gap behaviour with a post-gap docstring on top.

2. THE PROMPT FILES ARE INCONSISTENT IN DEPTH ACROSS THE SAME ROUND. Gap 47's StatCard.prompt.md was rewritten in full — prop table, migration paragraph, five worked examples. Gap 37's Button.prompt.md, IconButton.prompt.md and Menu.prompt.md were not touched at all, and Select.prompt.md / OptionCardGroup.prompt.md still show bare `disabled: true` options. The capability, the .d.ts, the law and the dedicated spec card all landed in both cases; only the per-component prompt did not, and it is the file a drawing agent opens first when it is drawing a button rather than researching a ruling.

3. THE HOST LIST FOR NamedGap DISAGREES WITH ITSELF ACROSS FILES. readme.md law 10 and SKILL.md both name four hosts including `CompareGrid`'s `attribute.gapLabel`; NamedGap.d.ts and NamedGap.prompt.md name three and omit it. 4. gaps.evidence: THE CONFLATION IS GONE FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION, NOT JUST THE TYPE. The audit's exact line — `const good = deltaDir === "up";` — no longer exists anywhere in StatCard.jsx. In its place: `const SENTIMENTS = { good: { bg: "var(--success-bg)", fg: "var(--success-text)", word: "better" }, bad: { bg: "var(--danger-bg)", fg: "var(--danger-text)", word: "worse" }, neutral: { bg: "var(--neutral-bg)", fg: "var(--neutral-text)", word: null } };` resolved from the caller's prop only: `const sent = SENTIMENTS[deltaSentiment] || SENTIMENTS.neutral; const sentWord = sentimentLabel || sent.word;`. The signature carries both facts with the correct default: `delta, deltaDir = "up", deltaSentiment = "neutral", sentimentLabel, band,`. TWO FACTS, TWO CHANNELS, IN THE RENDER. Direction is the glyph and nothing else: `{deltaDir === "flat" ? : deltaDir === "down" ? : }` — `flat` really is a bar, so a zero delta asserts no direction. Sentiment is the tint AND a word, satisfying F7-12: `background: sent.bg, color: sent.fg` plus `{sentWord && <>·{sentWord}}`. Direction is also spoken: `const dirWord = deltaDir === "down" ? "Down" : deltaDir === "flat" ? "No change" : "Up";` rendered as `{dirWord} `. THE TYPE SAYS THE SAME THING. gaps.refuteWhy: I tried to break this and could not. The register's LIVE evidence names one line — `const good = deltaDir === "up";` — and it is gone from StatCard.jsx, replaced by a map resolved from the caller's prop alone: `const SENTIMENTS = { good: {bg:"var(--success-bg)", fg:"var(--success-text)", word:"better"}, bad: {...danger..., word:"worse"}, neutral: {bg:"var(--neutral-bg)", fg:"var(--neutral-text)", word:null} };` then `const sent = SENTIMENTS[deltaSentiment] || SENTIMENTS.neutral;`. Signature: `delta, deltaDir = "up", deltaSentiment = "neutral", sentimentLabel, band,`. Direction is the glyph only (`deltaDir === "flat" ? : deltaDir === "down" ? ... : ...`) plus `{dirWord} `; sentiment is `background: sent.bg, color: sent.fg` plus `{sentWord && <>·{sentWord}}`. .d.ts agrees verbatim ("**Which way the figure moved, and nothing more.**" / "**Default `neutral`, deliberately.**"). I then checked every teaching surface the claim did NOT open, which is where this audit's partials always hide: - **`_adherence.oxlintrc.json`** (the enforced prop contract, unread by them): `" doesn't accept that prop. Declared props: label, value, unit, money, compact, gap, delta, deltaDir, deltaSentiment, sentimentLabel, band, ..."` plus two enum rules — `" deltaDir must be one of 'up' | 'down' | 'flat'."` and `" deltaSentiment must be one of 'good' | 'bad' | 'neutral'."`. The lint layer is not stale. - **All three templates, including the halves that never render** (`templates/app-layout/app.jsx`, `desktop-web-app/app.jsx`, `mobile-field-app/app.jsx` — I read both `Desktop()` and `Mobile()` in each): none destructures `StatCard` from the namespace at all, so there is no template teaching the old form. - **Eight further spec cards that host StatCard**: `named-gaps.card.html` (`delta="12%" deltaDir="up" deltaSentiment="good"`), `banded-figure.card.html` (`deltaDir="up" deltaSentiment="good"` beside `deltaDir="up" deltaSentiment="bad"`), `blocks.card.html`, `unavailable-state.card.html`, `derivation.card.html` (no delta), plus `money-summary.card.html`, `app-shell.card.html`, `data-composites.card.html`, `attribution.card.html`, `charts.card.html` (no StatCard delta). All clear 4.5. I also checked the mode the claim never looked at: `tokens/field-mode.css` darkens only the `-text` partners and leaves the `-bg` tints untouched, so in high-contrast field mode the new default chip is `#3A3D42` on `#F0F1F3` = **9.65:1** — the default gets safer, not worse. What the retrievable prefix does show is BandedFigure's compiled docstring already reasoning about the post-split prop — "`deltaSentiment` judges the DELTA… Sentiment is a closed triple whose words are fixed (better / worse / nothing)" — so the bundle post-dates the change. That is direction inference, not the good/bad inference the gap forbids. (2) `BandedFigure.jsx`'s header comment calls word+mark+tint "the same three channels StatusChip, Provenance and **StatCard's sentiment** use" — sentiment has two channels (tint + word); the arrow is deliberately direction-only. `BandedFigure.prompt.md` states it correctly, so the slip is confined to a source comment. gaps.crossCutting:
THREE NEIGHBOUR CONFLICTS AND ONE STALE ENFORCEMENT PAGE.

1. THE TOUCH-TARGETS CARD'S INVENTORY IS STALE — 11 of 59 specimen cards are never swept. guidelines/touch-targets.card.html exists, and it does measure live rather than grep: it opens each card in an iframe, reads React fibre props (`function fibreProps(el) { for (const k in el) if (k.startsWith("__reactProps$")) return el[k]; }`), measures `el.getBoundingClientRect()`, resolves a visually-hidden input to its `<label>`, and prints a verdict against `const MIN = 44`. That machinery is sound, and it is registered in _ds_manifest.json ("guidelines/touch-targets.card.html | Spacing | Touch targets — measured").

But its headline claim — "it opens EVERY specimen card in the system in an iframe" — is false. Its `CARDS` array lists 48 component cards; the project ships 59. Diffed against the live file list, these are absent from both `CARDS` and `PHONE`: components/charts/pin-placement, components/data/banded-figure, components/data/checklist, components/data/derivation, components/data/money-summary, components/feedback/disclosure, components/feedback/generate-gate, components/feedback/pending-and-progress, components/forms/money-and-held-photos, components/print/drawing-sheet, components/print/paged-document. All eleven are registered cards in _ds_manifest.json, so they are live specimens in the pane, not orphans.

This is not a cosmetic omission. I opened components/feedback/pending-and-progress.card.html to check: it is one of the most control-dense cards in the system — DataTable `rowActions` Assign buttons, PendingAction `onRetry`/`onDismiss` link buttons, ListRow's "Undo", Kanban move buttons, JobTray `onCancel`/`onClear`, OperationProgress `onCancel`/`onRetry`, AppHeader's bell and avatar — and it renders a `.phone` block at `width:375px`. The PendingAction retry/dismiss and the JobTray cancel are exactly the small text-button targets the 44px floor exists to catch, on exactly the phone form where the in-row exception does not apply. Same for checklist (tick controls), disclosure and derivation (toggles), generate-gate (buttons), pin-placement (pin placement controls). The page that is meant to be the enforcement is silently exempting them.

2. HOSTS DISAGREE ON WHAT `provenance` ACCEPTS, AND ChartFrame MANGLES THE CASE IT DOES NOT DECLARE. ListRow.d.ts, Block.d.ts and ActivityStream.d.ts type it `ProvenanceProps | ProvenanceTierSpec | React.ReactNode`; DataTable.d.ts (table-wide, `column.provenance`, `provenanceFor`, `rowProvenance`, `totalRow.provenance`), RecordCardProps and ChartFrameProps all type it `ProvenanceProps | ProvenanceTierSpec` with no node. At runtime the shared helper accepts a node everywhere — Provenance.jsx `renderProvenance` opens with `if (React.isValidElement(spec)) return spec;` — so the runtime is uniform and the declarations are not.

ChartFrame is worse than inconsistent, it is wrong. Charts.jsx pre-processes before delegating:
`provenance && typeof provenance === "object" && !React.isValidElement(provenance) ? { ...provenance, standing: … } : (provenance || standing || …) ? { tier: provenance, standing, source, projection, note } : null`
A ready `<Provenance>` element fails the `!React.isValidElement` guard and falls into the else branch, landing in `tier`. `resolveTier` then hits `if (typeof tier === "object")` and returns `{ label: tier.label || null || "", color: … || "var(--text-tertiary)" }` — an element has no `.label`. `Provenance.isEmpty` is therefore false, and the frame renders a bare grey dot with an empty word: a provenance carried by colour alone, which is the one thing F8-07 forbids. This was flagged in the previous round and is unchanged.

3. FIELDOVERRIDE DOES NOT KNOW IT GAINED A HOST. 15A routed SCR-M07-13's rep-corrected into FieldOverride via `NextAction.correction`, but FieldOverride's own teaching surfaces still enumerate the old three: FieldOverride.d.ts closes with "Hosts: `NumberField`, `Input`, and `DataTable` via `column.override` — `MS10-18`'s eleven editable BOM columns get one treatment instead of 440 improvisations", and FieldOverride.jsx's docstring likewise cites only M05-72 / MS10-13 / M05-65 and "NumberField and Input had no overridden flag". A designer reading FieldOverride to decide whether it is the right treatment for a corrected task will not learn that it already is one. Doc-only — the wiring works — but it is the same left-behind-teaching-surface shape.

4. THE ACTOR-CLASS HOST COUNT IS ONE BEHIND. ActorClass.d.ts says "one vocabulary now serves three hosts: `ActivityStream.entry.actorClass`, `NextAction.origin`, and `Transcript`'s turns", and readme.md line 109 repeats "now has **three hosts**". There are four: Checklist.d.ts declares `doneBy?: ActorClassSpec;` — "**Who ticked it** (`MS11-35`) — an `ActorClass` spec… Not a second person-glyph" — and readme.md line 279 itself names it ("**Attribution is `ActorClass`'s job**"). The behaviour is correct and consistent; only the enumeration is stale, and it contradicts another line of the same readme.

5. "ATTRIBUTION" NOW NAMES TWO DIFFERENT AXES IN ONE API SURFACE, which is worth knowing before 99 screens are drawn. `DataTableColumn.attribution` and ListRow's `attribution` mean ValueSource (which layer supplied the value); ActorClass means who or what acted, and its slot on a task is called `origin`; the card at components/data/attribution.card.html is registered as "Value attribution" while components/data/task-attribution.card.html is "Why this task exists". Each slot is distinct and the d.ts files keep them mutually exclusive, so nothing is broken — but the shared word invites a designer to reach for the wrong one.

1. THE LOCK BREAKS THE COMPONENT'S OWN FOCUS LAW. ReorderList.jsx restores focus after a delete with `const at = keys[Math.min(p.index, keys.length - 1)]; const el = at != null ? btns.current[`${at}:delete`] : null; if (el) el.focus(); else if (listRef.current) listRef.current.focus();`. The delete ref is registered only inside `{deletable(it, i) && ...}`. ScopeNote is the one whose headline sentence — "The act is absent" — a statutory row also matches, so the prompt that most needs the disambiguation is the one that lacks it.

The title was patched from "two"; the body was not.

"var(--accent-subtle)" : "var(--surface)"` after a move. #6B6E74 on #EEECFF computes to 4.40:1, under the P0 floor readme and tokens/colors.css both state as "Every token that sets WORDS clears 4.5:1". Conceded defect the claimant already named (ReorderList.prompt.md's first example passing an event handler to `Textarea`, whose Textarea.d.ts signature is `onChange?: (value: string) => void`) is real and I confirmed it; it is the fourth-most serious item here, not the only one.

Verdict: PARTIAL. The capability and its API exist; the teaching surfaces do not all agree, and `lockOf` silently violates the focus contract its own docs state three times.

gaps.crossCutting:
Three contradictions across this slice and its neighbours.

1. ONE LAW, TWO SPELLINGS — aria-busy across the four PendingAction hosts (gap 42). DataTable.jsx (`const waiting = !!(pending && pending.state !== "returned")`) and Kanban.jsx (`aria-busy={pending && pending.state !== "returned" ? "true" : undefined}`) treat an omitted `state` as waiting; ListRow.jsx and NextAction.jsx/RecordCard insert an extra `&& pending.state` and therefore emit nothing for the default spec `{label: "…"}`. PendingAction.d.ts declares `state?: "waiting" | "returned"` with waiting as the default and says "Hosts set `aria-busy` on the row"; readme law 11 says "`aria-busy` and never `aria-invalid`". Four hosts, one treatment, two answers — and the failing pair is the phone pair, on the screens (SCR-M02-02 triage, SCR-M02-06 merge) the gap was raised for.

2. THE NEW LAW INDICTS A COMPONENT NOBODY REVISITED. Gap 51's fix added a clause to readme.md §4: "**And a component that owns a breakpoint has to publish it.**" Three components own a breakpoint and answer the publishing question three different ways. Kanban publishes via a callback prop, `onFormChange({stacked, width})`. EditorSurface publishes via a hook plus a function child, `useEditorForm()` → `{ref, layerWidth, panel, probeStyle}` and `children({panel, layerWidth})`. DataTable publishes nothing at all: DataTable.jsx:44-45 runs its own `new ResizeObserver(([e]) => setW(e.contentRect.width))`, DataTable.jsx:109 computes `const stacked = ownWidth !== null && ownWidth < stackBelow;`, and DataTableProps declares `stackBelow?: number` with no callback and no exposed measurement. A screen that needs to know whether its 40-line BOM is a table or a stack of cards — to place a "continued" header, a total line, or a phone-only action above it — has to duplicate the observer, which is verbatim the failure the clause was written to forbid. Either the law needs a stated boundary or DataTable needs the same publication.

3. THE .JSX AND THE .D.TS DISAGREE ABOUT THE MARKET FORMAT (gap 48). `createFormat` in format.js returns `{ … currencySymbol, symbolPosition: p.symbolPosition, … }`, NumberField.jsx reads both off `useFormat()`, and the `MarketFormat` interface in MarketProvider.d.ts declares neither. This is the same failure mode the audit exists to catch, one layer down: the component carries the right behaviour and the declared contract of the thing it consumes says that behaviour is unreachable. It is not confined to gap 48 — any future component that needs to render a currency symbol beside a value (a money cell in DataTable, an amount in a MoneySummary line) will read the type, conclude the symbol is not available from the format object, and bake one in, which is exactly the "no component owns a currency" rule that format.js's own comment says the derivation exists to protect.

TWO CSS-LAYER OMISSIONS, both of which break the surface's central claim on actual paper.

(1) THERE IS NO `@page` RULE ANYWHERE IN THE SYSTEM. I read tokens/print.css end to end — it has `:root{...}`, `[data-print="print-only"]{display:none}` and one `@media print{...}` block containing `html,body`, `*`, the three `data-print` rules, `[data-print-chrome]`, `.hg-sheet`, `.hg-sheet-stack`, `[data-keep-together]`, `thead`, `tfoot`, `h1,h2,h3,p` and `a`. No `@page`, no `size`, no `margin: 0`. tokens/base.css has no `@page` and no `@media print` at all; tokens/typography.css has none; and readme.md line 84 names print.css as "the system's only `@media print` block", so there is nowhere else it could live.

Both print.css and readme.md law 14 assert the payoff — print.css: "One sheet, one page. The cut is computed in JS and emitted as explicit sheets, so the browser has nothing left to decide"; readme law 14: "Print has nothing left to decide (one sheet is one page, `tokens/print.css`)". That is only true with `@page { size: <paper>; margin: 0 }`. Without it the browser applies its own default page margin (~10mm in Chrome), so the printable box on A4 is roughly 190×277mm while `.hg-sheet` is a hard `width: 794px; height: 1123px` — exactly 210×297mm. Every sheet is larger than the page box in BOTH axes, so `break-inside: avoid` cannot be honoured and each emitted sheet fragments onto a second physical page: a full page plus a sliver. That reproduces precisely the duplicate and blank pages MS9-02 forbids ("sequential unique page numbers, no duplicates, and no trailing blank page in the PDF"), and it defeats obligation (1)'s "pixel-for-content identical" — the counted footer will say "Sheet 3 of 7" on a PDF holding 14 physical pages.

DrawingSheet is affected harder: `export function DrawingSheet({ paper = "a4", orientation = "landscape", ...})` — landscape by default, so `g.width` is 1123 and `g.height` 794. With no `@page { size: A4 landscape }` it prints onto a portrait page and is clipped at 794px wide. MS8-02's "paper size, scale and sheet numbering consistent across every sheet and title block" is stated correctly in the title block and contradicted by the actual output.

(2) `data-print-chrome` IS DECLARED BUT SET BY NOTHING. tokens/print.css: `/* Operator chrome — rail, header, bottom nav, toolbars — is never part of a customer artefact. */ [data-print-chrome]{display:none!important}`. 1. THE SCOPE LINE DISAPPEARS EXACTLY WHERE GAP 46 MEETS GAP 32 — the one real defect at a seam. DataTable's honesty rule against a total that sums more lines than are visible fires only on the pager path: `useTotal` computes `const paged = typeof page === "number" && (rowCount ?? rows.length) > pageSize; const scope = t.scope ?? (paged ? \`all ${rowCount ?? rows.length} lines\` : null);`. When PagedDocument cuts a BOM across sheets it calls `it.section.renderRows(it.rows.slice(p.from, p.to), ctx)` — DataTable receives `rows={chunk}` and no `page`/`pageSize`/`rowCount`, so `paged` is false and no scope line renders. The canonical example reproduces the failure: paged-document.card.html passes `rows={chunk}` with `totalRow={last ? {label: "Bill of materials total", ... } : undefined}` and no `scope`, so on the final sheet a 22-line BOM's total prints under whatever few rows landed there, with nothing saying it covers all 22. That is precisely the "lie by adjacency" DataTable.d.ts says the scope line exists to prevent ("a total under ten visible rows that sums forty is a lie by adjacency") — defeated on paper, in the surface whose whole claim is that paper and screen are identical. The fix is already available: `renderRows`'s ctx carries `count`, so the card and any screen copying it should pass `scope={\`all ${count} lines\`}`. Because the card is what 99 screens will copy, this propagates.

2. THE PAPER INK COLOURS ARE RAW HEX LITERALS WHILE THE RULE COLOUR WAS TOKENISED — an inconsistency inside the print surface itself. tokens/print.css defines `--doc-fs`, `--doc-fs-small`, `--doc-fs-figure`, `--doc-lh`, `--sheet-gap`, `--sheet-radius` and `--doc-rule:rgba(10,10,11,0.10)`, but no ink token. "#0A0A0B" : "var(--text-primary)"`), Disclosure.jsx and both print cards. F7-03 forbids raw colour literals ("every visual value reaches a screen through the design system, never by transcription"), and gap 34 in the register is an open gap about exactly this class of omission. I measured all three inks against white and they pass, so this is token hygiene rather than an accessibility failure: #6B6E74 → 5.10:1, #54565B → 7.34:1, #0A0A0B → ~19.9:1. A `--doc-ink` / `--doc-ink-quiet` / `--doc-ink-faint` trio beside `--doc-rule` would close it. Note the system is light-only (`tokens/base.css`: `:root{ color-scheme:light; }`), which is why the hardcoded near-black does not currently misfire in the `rendering="web"` branch, where `<DisclosureSet items={disclosures} surface="document" />` is hardcoded to document surface regardless of rendering.

3. tokens/print.css CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE TYPE FLOOR, in the same paragraph. It states "a sheet is real paper, so these are stated in pt as well and the reading floor is 12pt", then immediately defines `--doc-fs-small 14px = 10.5pt` for "title-block metadata, the foot of a sheet, a legend row" and closes with "Nothing on a sheet goes below --doc-fs-small". gaps.component: AllocationMeter — parts against an exact target, remainder in words, over-allocation drawn past a target line
gaps.evidence:
WHAT LANDED — the gap's stated requirement is met in full.
`components/feedback/AllocationMeter.jsx` renders the remainder as content, not as a gap in a bar:
  `const words = remainderWords != null ? remainderWords : !resolved ? unresolvedNote : st === "met" ? "Fully allocated." : st === "over" ? `${nfmt(sum - target)}${unit} over-allocated.` : `${nfmt(target - sum)}${unit} unallocated.`;`
Over-allocation is drawable because the track is not clamped:
  `const scale = Math.max(target, resolved ? sum : target) || 1;`
  and each part splits at the target line — `const inside = Math.max(0, Math.min(v, target - run)); const beyond = Math.max(0, v - inside);` — with the excess painted `var(--warning)` and a target tick drawn `{st === "over" && (<span … left: `calc(${tickAt}% - 1px)` …/>)}`.
`targetLabel` carries M06-13's rule verbatim in the card (`targetLabel="Total allocation must = 100%"`), and `enforcement = "at-generate"` is the default, writing "Generate is blocked until the allocation reaches 100%." The 375px requirement is honoured by `showLegend = false` by default ("at 375px the bar and the words come first").
Teaching surfaces agree: `readme.md` law 18 — "`ProgressBar` is the 6px drawing and nothing else… and it **clamps at 100**, so a rep whose rows add to 118% saw a full bar and no excess at all, which is half the failure the live feedback exists to catch. `AllocationMeter` is that meter." `AllocationMeter.prompt.md` carries the three-state table and the UsageMeter boundary. The @dsCard `allocation-meter.card.html` builds SCR-M06-09's step 7 at a literal `width: 375` with tranche rows + ＋ Add tranche + the meter, and renders `<ProgressBar value={118}/>` beside it as the labelled counter-example.

TWO DEFECTS I MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED — neither blocks a screen being drawn.

(a) `met` is decided by FLOAT STRICT EQUALITY, so a legitimate 100% split can render a zero-sized failure.
  `const st = state || (!resolved ? "under" : sum > target ? "over" : sum === target ? "met" : "under");`
I ran the real reducer over plausible splits. Eleven of twelve land exactly on 100 and read "Fully allocated." But a seven-tranche even split — 14.28/14.28/14.29/14.29/14.28/14.29/14.29 — sums in float64 to **99.99999999999997**, so `sum === target` is false, the state falls to `under`, and `nfmt(target - sum)` rounds the shortfall to zero. The meter renders **"0% unallocated."** with the enforcement line "Generate is blocked until the allocation reaches 100%." — a rep is told to fix a shortfall of nothing, on the exact screen whose purpose is live feedback. Nothing upstream prevents it: the card's own tranche input is `<NumberField density="functional" value={p.value} min={0} max={100} unit="%" steppers={false} …/>` with no `precision`, so decimals commit verbatim, and `＋ Add tranche` puts no ceiling on row count. An epsilon comparison (or rounding `sum` to `unit` precision before the three-way test) is the fix.

(b) The `over` MARK misses the system's own non-text contrast floor, and contradicts how every neighbour draws the same thing.
  `function Mark({ state }) { const c = state === "met" ? "var(--success)" : state === "over" ? "var(--warning)" : "var(--mark-subtle)"; … background: c, color: "var(--text-inverse)" …}`
Computed from the live `tokens/colors.css` (`--warning:#E9A23B`, `--surface:#FFFFFF`, `--text-inverse:#FFFFFF`): the amber circle is **2.17:1** against the white pane it sits on, and the white "+" glyph inside it is **2.17:1** against the amber — both below WCAG's 3:1 non-text floor, which `readme.md` states as law: "Where a mark carries meaning on a tint — a `StatusChip` dot, an attendance marker, a provenance tier — it uses the `-text` partner too, **since the plain token misses even the 3:1 non-text floor there**." The `met` mark is fine (white tick on `--success` #159A5B = 3.62:1). Using `--warning-text` #7A4F0B would give 7.12:1 on white. The words beside the mark are correct (`wordColour` uses `--warning-text`, measured 6.53–7.12:1), so meaning is not lost and F7-12 still holds — this is a legibility defect on a roof in sunlight, which is the readme's own stated worst case, not a missing capability.
(I verified every ratio in `tokens/colors.css` rather than accepting them; all its claimed figures reproduce to ±0.02.)

gaps.refuteWhy:
Everything the claimant quoted is true — I re-read both files and confirmed it. What they never tested is the one prop they did not quote: `order`. It is the prop that serves MS11-07, one of the twelve PRD rows the register binds, and it does not do what all three of its teaching surfaces say it does.

**1. `order="given"` does not preserve the given order (.d.ts and .jsx disagree; the card teaches the wrong output as correct).**

The claim: FindingList.d.ts — `order?: "severity" | "given";` documented as "`severity` (default) · `given` — `MS11-07`'s four *ordered* items **keep their order**." FindingList.jsx repeats it: "`given` = the caller's order, e.g. MS11-07's four ordered items."

The code: ordering is computed, then thrown away by an unconditional split.
```js
const ordered = order === "severity" ? [...list].sort(...) : list;
const open  = ordered.filter((f) => statusOf(f) !== "ready");
const ready = ordered.filter((f) => statusOf(f) === "ready");
```
`open` and `ready` render as two separate sibling `<ul>`s, open first. So `given` preserves the caller's order only *within* the open subset and *within* the ready subset — never across the set. Any set that interleaves a ready item is reordered.

MS11-07's set interleaves by definition, and the card's own MS11-07 panel is that case. `generate-gate.card.html` passes `<FindingList order="given" readyMode="listed" ...>` with items 1 ready / 2 attention / 3 blocking / 4 ready, captioned **"Given order, every item listed"**. Executed against the exact jsx logic:
- caller's order: `Design signed off | Payment 1 not received | No net-metering application | Materials in stock`
- actually rendered: `Payment 1 not received | No net-metering application | Design signed off | Materials in stock`

The register's evidence quotes MS11-07 as "four **ordered** items… each with the step that can fix it, three statuses, and a worst-of verdict", and the gap headline is "an **ordered** set of issues". `readyMode="listed"` is passed precisely to stop the default folding those two ready items — and the workaround still delivers 2,3,1,4. A designer drawing SCR-MS-16 from this card gets a handover checklist whose dependency order is scrambled, with a caption telling them it is right. This is the round's usual failure mode inverted: the docstring and the card are wrong about the code, not behind it.

**2. The severity mark contradicts a named readme law, recomputed from tokens/colors.css.**

readme.md, the marks-vs-words law: "Where a mark carries meaning on a tint — **a `StatusChip` dot**, an attendance marker, a provenance tier — **it uses the `-text` partner too**, since the plain token misses even the 3:1 non-text floor there." `guidelines/color-contrast.card.html` states the number: "`--warning` as words on `--warning-bg` measures **1.99:1**."

I recomputed: **1.99:1**. `StatusChip` — the exemplar the law names — draws its dot as `background: t.c` where `TONES.warning = { c: "var(--warning-text)" ... }`, and passes. FindingList follows `BandChip` (`background: t.mark`) instead of the law's cited model.

The per-row `Mark` disc compounds it: 18px `background: s.mark` on `var(--surface)` → `#E9A23B` on `#FFFFFF` = **2.17:1**, under the 3:1 non-text floor; and the glyph inside is `color: "var(--text-inverse,#fff)"` → white on `#E9A23B` = **2.17:1**, while the readme sanctions `--text-inverse` only "on a dark or accent fill" (19.79 on `--action-primary`, 5.41 on `--accent`). `attention` is one of the three statuses M05-58 names, so this is the second channel for a third of the vocabulary, on a product whose readme names "mid-range Android phones on a roof in direct sunlight" as the design condition. (danger 3.91/3.43 and success 3.62/3.28 clear 3:1; only the amber fails, and it fails on both surfaces.)

**Minor, noted not charged:** `--accent-text` does not exist in tokens/colors.css, so the inline-fix button's `color: "var(--accent-text,var(--accent))"` resolves to `--accent` `#5A4BFF` on `--accent-subtle` `#EEECFF` = 4.65:1 — passes 4.5 for 14px/600 by 0.15. gaps.refuteWhy:
The claim's headline sentence — "Every clause of M05-76 / MS11-35 / MS11-30 / MS10-10 is in the item type" — is false, and its second headline ("IT PRINTS") is contradicted by the system's own print contract and by a number nobody measured.

WHAT LANDS (verified, not conceded on the claimant's word). Grouping is real: `(phases||[]).forEach((p)=>{const k=p.id||p.label; groups.set(k,[]); order.push(k);})` then `order.filter((k)=>(groups.get(k)||[]).length>0).map(...)` — one heading per group, MS11-30's non-repetition is structural. No optimistic flip is real: I read the whole file; there is no `useState` anywhere in Checklist.jsx, `<TickBox done={item.done}/>` reads only the prop, and `renderPending`/`renderActorClass` both exist with the signatures claimed (`if (typeof spec === "string") return <ActorClass actorClass={spec} {...extra} />;` in ActorClass.jsx). Count-with-meaning is real. Toggle hit box measures 44×44 exactly (`minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44`); MS10-10's evidence anchor is a real `<a href>` at `minHeight: 44`. Tick contrast recomputed from tokens/colors.css: white #FFFFFF on `--success` #159A5B = 3.62:1 (passes the 3:1 non-text floor); the pen box's `--mark-subtle` #83888E rule = 3.57:1. Card is in _ds_manifest.json; `Checklist` is in the bundle's component list. d.ts and jsx agree on every prop.

MISS 1 — HALF OF MS11-35's ATTRIBUTION IS NOT BUILT, AND readme LAW 23 TRUNCATES THE QUOTE SO IT CANNOT BE SEEN. The register's own evidence (DESIGN-SYSTEM-GAPS.md:869-879) reads "carry R16 attribution — **who ticked, optional 'done by'**", and M05-76 in ux/briefs/SCR-MS-17: "In v1 the coordinator runs the checklist and ticks are attributed to them **with an optional free-text 'done by'** (R16 via F2, cited)" — the crew has no login in v1, so these are two facts: the coordinator who ticked, and a free-text name of whoever actually did the work. `ChecklistItem` has exactly one slot: `doneBy?: ActorClassSpec`, documented in the .d.ts as "**Who ticked it** (`MS11-35`)". There is no second field. A screen drawing SCR-MS-17's `progress-ticks` state ("who ticked plus optional 'done by'") must either drop the ticker or drop the crew name. The only workaround is stuffing it into `doneAt` (the card already abuses that slot: `doneAt:"auto-ticked from the survey"`), which is undocumented and unlabelled. Now the teaching surfaces: Checklist.jsx's own docstring quotes the clause in full — "carry attribution — who ticked, optional 'done by'" — and the component does not implement it; Checklist.prompt.md and the .d.ts drop the clause silently; and readme law 23 quotes MS11-35 as *"...and carry attribution — **who ticked**"*, cutting the sentence off immediately before ", optional 'done by'" and also dropping "R16". That is the exact failure mode this audit exists for: the law was rewritten to match what was built.

MISS 2 — THE PRINTED FORM IS A SECOND, PRIVATE PRINT MECHANISM THAT A REAL PRINT NEVER REACHES. tokens/print.css states the contract outright: "PRINT SCOPING RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and **this is the whole contract** ... `data-print="screen-only"` / `"print-only"` / `"always"`", enforced by readme law 15 ("it prints undefeatably — `data-print="always"` plus `PrintScope`'s hoist"). Checklist.jsx contains **zero `data-print` attributes** and no PrintScope registration; its print behaviour is a React prop, `surface = "screen"` by default. So Ctrl-P on SCR-MS-17 prints the screen form — green ticks, 44px toggle buttons — and the pen-box form is reachable only through a prop the default does not set and no `@media print` rule can flip. `surface="document"` occurs exactly once in the whole readme (line 281), i.e. it is a novel second treatment of print scoping. The canonical example teaches the wrong thing rather than the fix: checklist.card.html demonstrates it with a hand-built `<button onClick={()=>setSurface(...)}>surface = {surface} — switch</button>`, and no teaching surface anywhere tells an author to render a `data-print="print-only"` document copy beside a `screen-only` screen copy.

MISS 3 — AN UNMEASURED NUMBER IN THE PRINTED FORM. tokens/print.css: "--doc-fs 16px = 12pt reading copy ... --doc-fs-small 14px = 10.5pt ... **Nothing on a sheet goes below --doc-fs-small**." The `doc` branch of Item() reuses the identical `body` node as the screen branch — no type change at all. Measured from the source: title 15px = 11.25pt, `S.detail` 13px = 9.75pt, `S.micro` 12px = 9pt (materials, attribution, progressNote), phase heading `S.h` 12px uppercase = 9pt. Every line of the paper field document a crew reads on a roof sits below the sheet floor, and the body copy is 9.75pt against a 12pt reading standard. `surface="document"` changes the tick box and the toggle and nothing else.

MISS 4 (minor, but it is the enforcement surface). guidelines/touch-targets.card.html is the system's own sweep — "it opens **every specimen card in the system** in an iframe ... measures the rendered rectangle" — and its `CARDS` and `PHONE` arrays do not contain `components/data/checklist.card.html`. The most phone-bound component in the system (SCR-MS-17, 375px, one-handed, on a roof) is absent from the phone pass, so its 44px claims have never been measured by the instrument that exists to measure them.

Not found, having looked: no .d.ts/.jsx disagreement, no contradicting neighbour (FindingList and ComplianceFloor do not overlap; Timeline/Checkbox/ProgressBar are correctly named as rejected), no stale template (the three templates do not render a checklist), and MS11-28/29 are marked "non-UI half, build-side — for awareness, not for drawing" so their absence is legitimate.

gaps.component: Derivation + DerivationGroup in components/data/, beside Provenance
gaps.evidence: PRESENT — the gap's core demand ("readable by touch and by a screen reader as ADJACENT CONTENT rather than as a hover") is met structurally, not by styling. The trigger is `<button type="button" onClick={toggle} aria-expanded={isOpen} aria-controls={panelId} style={{ ... minHeight: 44 ... }}>` and the panel is its next sibling in normal flow, `<div id={panelId} ...>`, under the comment "the accessibility difference from a tooltip is not the styling, it is that this is focusable, tappable at 44px, and its content lands in the flow." The four kinds map one-to-one onto the PRD rows: `DerivationKind = "formula" | "assumption" | "boundary" | "exclusion" | "note"` documented as M05-72's formula in words, MS6-47's "nominal — engineer to confirm", MS7-22's model boundary, and exclusions. F8-07 is protected by an ABSENCE: `DerivationProps` has no `tier`, and the d.ts says why — "passing one would let a caller retire a persistent label behind a disclosure, the exact thing `F8-07` forbids" — and Provenance.d.ts back-references it ("This is the label; the argument is `Derivation`... which sits under this line and never replaces it"), so the two neighbours agree. Forty-on-a-BOM is answered: closed by default, `DerivationGroup` holds one `openId`, and print uses the system's own vocabulary from tokens/print.css — inline panels `data-print={group && group.printAppendix ? "screen-only" : undefined}` and the appendix `<section data-print="print-only">`. derivation.card.html mounts it in a real BOM table inside a `<DerivationGroup>` and beside a `<Provenance tier="derived" ... />` on a StatCard, with a `<Tooltip>` shown as the counter-example; readme law 24 and prompt.md say the same. Card registered in the manifest. DEFECT — `mode="many"` is a declared prop the implementation cannot honour: `DerivationGroupProps { mode?: "single" | "many"; ... }` but jsx has `const setOpen = React.useCallback((id) => setOpenId(mode === "single" ? id : id), [mode]);` — both branches of the ternary return `id`, and the state is a single `openId`, so opening a second panel always closes the first. A caller writing `<DerivationGroup mode="many">` gets single-open silently.
gaps.stillMissing: `mode="many"` is inert. Nothing outside the .d.ts type ever describes what it should do — prompt.md and readme law 24 only say "single-open by default" and "there is no `openAll`" — so the type is the sole promise and it is unimplemented. It matters on SCR-MS-10's model-boundary panel and SCR-MS-03's provenance footer, where two or three explanations open together is reasonable and the 40-line constraint that motivates single-open does not apply. Either implement it (an open-id Set) or delete the union member so the API stops offering it.
